['I purchased this $50 Apple Gift card on Prime Day at the sale price of $40.00.  Once I received it, I pealed off the strip to reveal the redemption code.  The card must have been old or stored in the heat as the peal removed most of the first three characters of the redemption code.I could not read it.  Apples redemption scanner couldn\'t read it either.  What do you do with a card that you can not redeem?  I decided to try Apple support.  They require you to email them along with images of both sides of the card and my receipt.  Simple enough?  Nope.  Safari on my Mac would not let me attach it to the email as required.  I then redid the email on an iPad, re-took the images and successfully added the card images.  But not the Amazon receipt.  It would not accept a pdf or image of the receipt.  I ended up taking a screen print of the receipt.  That worked.  Now I must wait on the generosity of Apple to provide a new card.  If they refuse, I\'m out $40.  Clearly either Apple had a bad print on the card or Amazon did not store it properly and the strip adhesive was damaged.  The card does look and feel "old" but can\'t swear to it.  The moral of the story is don\'t buy gift cards.  Once you give up your money for them, you have no real recourse if the card can\'t be redeemed.  Buyer beware.']

Fortunately, after I made a subsequent purchase it magically reappeared.  This brief reappearance is why I was able to grab it this time, without repeating my foolish hesitation.  The terms for this offer state that only one offer, one time, per each individual account is ever available in a lifetime (I just paraphrased several lengthy bullet points).  So, get yours while this offer is still available. Let it rain free money from Amazon.com!!!']

review_texts_seq:
["I am a credit card guy. Unfortunately they are not accepted everywhere. This comes in handy for places that don't accept credit cards. Also it does work at gas stations after registering the card online.", "I have bought several of these gift cards for personal use. One of the reasons I buy these is because you can use them at stores that do not accept credit cards. You can assign a pin and use the card as a debit card. There is a grocery store that I like to shop at that will not accept credit cards but does accept visa debit gift cards such as this one. Again I think this is my 3rd or 4th card purchased from Amazon and up until this point I had no issues with this card.
So what happened?
There is a lot of fraud that happens with gift cards. They can be easily compromised. The gift card I purchased prior to this one did have a fraudulent charge on it. I caught it a few hours after it happened and called Paypal. They were able to stop the transaction and get me my money back. Understanding this, when I made any transactions with this card I made sure the card was not handed over to anyone. In early November I decided to check on my balance. The card was compromised. The last transaction was identical to the fraudulent charge mentioned above. A paypal charge leaving a few pennies left in the card. This gift card DOES have a way to dispute fraudulent charges. I downloaded the forms filled them out and e-mailed them to the e-mail address listed. A week later after receiving no response I sent another email inquiring on the status of my dispute. They e-mailed stating I need to send them the dispute form. I replied with the dispute form and explained I had sent it with my first e-mail. A week later no response. I sent it again to both emails asking for a status. Again no response. At this point it feels the ignorance is intentional.
So here's my suggestion.
Unless you use all the funds on this card within a month after purchasing it I don't recommend this card."]

["I really don't know why this requires a review... It's a gift card. Well, here goes anyway -
They ship very fast and come in a nice little box that makes it easy to give to someone. The gift card is a magnificent flexible plastic with beautiful print on the front (design of your choosing). It looks and smells like plastic too! Not that fake plastic either. It's definitely real plastic. I had it sent to a lab to verify this. I found out that the plastic itself added some value to the card beyond what was loaded on it (fraction of a cent).
It's thin and can easily be put in your wallet or purse without taking up too much space. A real treasure to own.

Cons: Despite their very high quality, these don't last very long. Rarely do they last more than a couple of weeks before their value drops to zero. I've heard stories of folks who have made them last longer but they're usually people dedicated to the task with a lot of will power. This was not the case for me.

Alternate Uses: Don't be fooled by the description, these cards have many uses before, during, and after their value plummets to zero. Here are a few things that I have used them for...
- Applying Drywall Patch Material
- Smoothing out Caulk in corners
- Cracking open laptops for repair
- Getting into a locked room in my house
- All purpose, non abrasive scraper
- Paint guard
- Makeshift Ninja Throwing Star
- Small protective mat for gluing things

*Please note that Amazon sells products to do all these things already but they don't fit in your wallet. These things are like Swiss Army Knives, conveniently saving me time by being readily accessible. Like any knife, remember to clean it when you're done using it."]

['I am a loyal Amazon customer. I have been a Prime member for years and so when it was time for my (now) husband and I to make a registry for our wedding, Amazon was an obvious option. As I searched through all the options of things to put on the registry, this popped up as a suggestion. My husband and I both work multiple jobs and money is always tight, so I figured if we were given this as a gift, it would be a nice excuse to get away for a weekend. Well, it turns out if people contribute money towards this in your registry, you don\'t actually get the gift cards. You are just given credit to Amazon. After 1 email, 2 different people on messenger, and 4 different people on the phone I was told it is illegal to use group gifting contributions on Amazon for a gift card to something else. When I said to the man "this makes no sense, why was this Massanutten gift card even an option then?" his response was "well, your guest got a pop-up box explicitly explaining the federal laws." I could be wrong but I think most times when we see a picture of a gift card and a title saying "Massanutten Gift Card" people think it is generally straight forward. Well, it\'s not.

Now if it is the case that all of this was because I had the group gifting tab checked to on, then my question is: why would amazon even allow that to be an option on gift cards to other places? Needless to say, the money my husband I and were going to use to take make step-son snow tubing is now sitting in my Amazon credit balance and I am unable to use it for Massanutten.

I hope this helps someone else out there before they make the same mistake I did because let me tell you, customer service will not help you.']

['I\'ll be honest, I didn\'t expect much nor did I even know this feature existed until a few minutes ago. I mainly wanted to use old pre-paid debit cards to pay for a "splurge" purchase. I was not offered nor did I expect to receive any of the rebates/rewards that other reviewers are talking about. At first I felt a bit mischievous, like.. is this ok? Am I doing something weird that I\'m not supposed to be doing, combining all these prepaid cards into one balance? And it was fine, for the first two cards, both prepaid Visa debit cards, and I was pretty happy when my email dinged and my balance was updated as expected. For the "name on card" data input I used "GIFT CARD RECIPIENT" for both and that worked out fine. One reviewer stated that the cards had to be registered prior to being used for this purpose. I registered one of them (it was a Wal-Mart branded gift card from Visa) and the other didn\'t have any obvious way of registering it so I didn\'t do anything, and both worked the same and took roughly the same amount of time to update in my account balance. Pretty cool way to use up prepaid debit cards with a miscellaneous balance, but....

The third try was not a charm, more like three strikes and I was out of luck. I tried using a prepaid AMEX, which happened to have the most value of the three cards (all were under $100), and it was declined. I read some reviews that said Amazon does an authorization check by dinging the card for $1 (Amazon\'s policy on prepaid cards also mentions this, it\'s not really a charge I guess? I\'m not a finance guy so I really don\'t know), and tried again using $1 less than the known value of the card. Still declined. Not sure what the reason is or could be. The email explaining the decline listed some standard reasons for why it might have declined. Interestingly, one of the reasons listed in that email was that the name on the card didn\'t match exactly what the bank had on file... being a gift card, there was no name on the card, though it did say "a gift for you" which I listed in the "name on card" data field for the first try. Then I tried a second time and entered "GIFT CARD RECIPIENT" in the name field, which worked for the previous two cards, but no luck this time around. Not sure what\'s up with that, not a big deal I guess, as I said I expected nothing going into this. Obviously other reviewers have pointed out some crazy stuff that happened to them, I\'d say be meticulous and pay attention to all the little details so you don\'t accidentally reload from your checking account when you don\'t mean to, but other than that my experience was positive.... 2/3 of the time. I\'ll make sure I update this review if I can make the third card work.']

["As others have mentioned, the ECA is a shady organization masquerading under the guise of an advocacy group for gaming rights and first amendment protections for videogames. Initially, the group offered a number of benefits as perks for membership, but of those, many are offers that you can get on one's own at any time (such as a free trial of Gamefly). The best perks have been dropped.

The greater problem is that in order to activate membership, you are required to provide a credit card number, even for a pre-purchased membership or a free membership (given through various promotions). They make it very easy to become a member. However, they make it nearly impossible to stop being a member. The ECA charges regular fees that you cannot get out of unless you cancel your member ship through a very specific form of WRITTEN correspondence (no e-mail or website help at all), and well in advance of your membership due date.

If you have recently become a member, I suggest you begin the proceedings to cancel now, and keep multiple copies of everything you send and receive. You might just get out of your contract by 2011."]

["I'm not sure if this is known or not but you can set up a gift card to be your main payment here on Amazon, set up refills with a credit card if it goes below a certain limit, have your digital rewards for shipping and stuff come to that same gift card, and skip having your credit card being a playground for price changes and rewards credit with Amazon.

I do my budget and the thing that frustrates me about stores and their price changes, such as WM and Amazon, is that I already calculated in my ledger for items when they do changes. Then I have to go in and find which line it was on, what was changed, calculate the difference, and create a new line item in my ledger. It's annoying for me and I was burning through line after line every week. Enter the gift card option for Amazon and I no longer need to worry about doing that. It's kind of like a store credit except it's my money that I put on there. And the fact that the company will put the rewards from shipping delay incentives on there and such is actually brilliant. I think WM needs to follow suit with this philosophy. Obviously, keep an eye on the price changes to make sure they're not going the other way to some extent but it's way less of a headache to just let Amazon do Amazon in Amazon's gift card thing. I love this idea and I think more companies need to follow suit."]

review_texts_seq: ['Okay I know there are a bunch of people in this thread that say “all you have to do is register the card and everything will be fine”. Well, that may be for a small % of the population however, what happened to me was that I purchased the card off of Amazon, then it arrived the next day. I opened it and immediately checked the balance online (I still have not registered it however at this point). The balance showed $200. I then proceeded to register it successfully and went to go to Target to do some shopping. When I used the card at checkout it kept getting declined for insufficient funds…So already beyond embarrassed I had to set my things aside while I checked the balance of the card again. To my horror and complete confusion the balance read $0.00, there had been several Google Play Store purchases and purchases from various other random online retailers that had completely wiped my card clean in a matter of an hour and a half….. I am not sure how someone is getting the card info in order to wipe the cards but it seems this is a common occurrence. Sadly only guess is that workers in the Amazon warehouses are somehow keeping track of these numbers and using them to wipe the cards before the customer has a chance to use them. MY SUGGESTION IS TO SAVE YOURSELF EVEN THE SLIGHTEST POSSIBLE HASSLE/LOSS BY NOT BUYING THESE CARDS FROM AMAZON!!!!!!!! Purchase them in person if you can, but the probability of scams when buying one here is pretty high….. Proceed at your own risk!']

This had me a bit worried that I had just paid $50 for an unloaded gift card. I opened the package so that I could get the code off the back of the card and check the balance on the website provided. Thankfully, the card IS loaded with the $50. I wish I would have left it in the package it came in because it would've looked better as a gift, but I felt I had to make sure it was actually loaded first. So learn from my mistake- yes, the card is loaded. And if you really want to be sure it is loaded, it provides a website you can go to to check the card balance. ["UPDATE TO THIS REVIEW: I am raising my rating from 4 stars to 5 because I have found a way to not use my gift card balance when I don't want to use it. Yay! For those of you who feel the same about this as I do, you can save your gift card balance up and make a purchase using your other payment methods. Click on the blue link in checkout to change your payment method. When you scroll all the way down the page you will find a small sentence saying to use the gift card balance for this purchase. There is a check box next to it and all you have to do is uncheck that box. You can then save your gift card balance for a different purchase you may be planning and the full price can be charged to whichever payment method you choose.

I love the fact that I am able to reload my gift card balance. It's a good feature. However, it's kind of awkward to do it. And it's not instantaneous. It can take up to 15 minutes.

My son wanted me to buy him a headset on Amazon. He handed me cash. I logged in to place an order for him. But I didn't want to spend my own gift card balance. But Amazon would have used that first on my purchase. I wanted to keep that on my account. So, instead of just buying his headset, I went in and loaded the amount I would need to the balance. Great. Except there was a delay. So I had to wait and reload the page. Then wait some more and reload the page again until finally the balance was available and I ordered his item. I'm no tech expert, but shouldn't there be an easier way to simply say that I don't want to use my gift card balance on a purchase?"]

review_texts_seq:
["I ordered this card in June and attempted to use it during dinner in November. The server came back to me with the gift card I had provided after trying to process the card unsuccessfully. When calling the number on the back of the card, apparently it wasn't open to help nor was there any way to check the balance on the card. Lots of time wasted but the staff at the restaurant came back after many attempts and stated the card had not been activated. So I call amazon customer service on the way home. Their call center in the pines was unable to located the order even when provided with the order number. After almost an hour on the phone, the representative found the problem was that the gift card had never been activated. I've been a loyal amazon.com customer but this its a major disappointment to see amazon sell a gift card that was never activated. Amazon's poor customer service by supervisor Rick who didn't even bother to understand what his subordinate had discovered only worsened a bad situation. The inconsistencies between the explanations also worsened the situation.

Beware buying any gift cards from Amazon as they may not be activated and put you an an embarrassing position with the check and waste hours of your time trying to explain the matter to customer service in another country.

Would give this experience negative stars if possible. Jeff I hope you are reading these reviews! I don't expect this type of experience with Amazon.com.

After some contemplation, I'm now wondering if gift cards previously purchased via Amazon and given as gifts may have not been activated - that would be even more embarrassing to learn about from friends."]

In my grandkids case, they will be holding real money, gift cards, and probably some Monopoly money, just to make them a little more fun.
These chocolate coin money holders are very well-made, the chocolate tastes pretty good, and they are so much fun! These will make great stocking stuffers, party favors, and good behavior or chore chart rewards, etc. I will be making these up as the Treasures for a Christmas scavenger hunt.

['This is a great addition to the various gift card options. Has the look and feel of a store bought gift card plus its value is customizable. Thanks Amazon!

I don\'t know why more companies don\'t do this. I was first introduced to this concept by "Talbots" so many years ago. Worked out great for last minute and spontaneous gifts. In a pinch for time, I would write the amount on the card, take a photo of the back of the card to capture data, mail it out, then go online that evening to load the card with funds. On one occasion, I sent my elderly Mother a gift card with a marked value of several hundred dollars. I didn\'t want to worry about it getting lost or misplaced, so I wrote instructions to call me the day prior to use. Worked out perfectly, she actually called me from the store minutes before making her purchases. I went online, loaded the card with funds and Mom was able to use the card minutes later.

This is vastly more convenient and secure than buying a gift card at your local store. So safe that you could freely carry these around in your wallet or purse or vehicle for that matter, even with a preselected amount already written on the card (the key is to write the amount on the back of the card as well and take a photo of the back, then use your smartphone to add funds and activate AFTER you\'ve given it out).
If you\'ve ever hesitated on sending a gift card to someone because you were concerned that the card may not arrive or be delivered to the wrong address or recipient, this flex card would place your worries aside. If you\'re sending one of these cards and want to make sure it\'s received by the intended individual, you could enclose a note instructing the recipient to "call, text or email (your contact information here) to activate this card" OR upon removal of the Amazon activation sticker (on the front of card), you could replace it with your own custom label, instructing recipient on who they need to contact to activate card. You could even add a field on the label for your own security question to recipient, how\'s that for multiple layers of security.

And NOW, my personal wish. When will Amazon be offering gift cards that are charged to the senders credit card at the time of REDEMPTION. (I wonder how many gift card purchases are wasting away in drawers or misplaced across the globe). Of course this would have to come with some notification function (similiar to auto renewal charge of subscriptions) but that would be kind of nice, knowing that your gift had just been used (no other details necessary other than possibly name of recipient)
Amazon could be the leader in this "Pay when they Redeem" concept.', "Couldn't go wrong, 25% savings with promo. A no brainer."]

["Hugely disappointing gift.

I'm not a big fan of gift cards in general, but I have received Amazon cards in the past. Amazon has a huge selection of items to purchase, great prices, and there were no problems activating and using my card - so that's fine. ... but that was Amazon, and Staples is not Amazon. By way of comparison, the Staples gift card has been a huge disappointment.

First, there is NO VALUE PRINTED ON THE CARD, so you have to go check the balance to even know what you have. Then when I went to the Staples website to check the cards balance, it kept telling me that the card number was invalid (though I verified both the card number and PIN were correctly entered several times, and even tried it a second and third time from another computer with a different browser). I was beginning to think I had a counterfeit card, but decided to re-check the card using the Staples 888 phone number, and that did work, so the card was fine. So the first disappointment was that Staples wasted over an hour of my time just trying to get the card to validate on the Staples website, only to find that the Staples website was screwed up for some reason, though the card was fine.

The Staples phone verification system reported that my card is a valid $25 giftcard, but once I was finally able to verify the cards balance using the phone system, I was in for another HUGE disappointment, because prices at Staples are so horrible that, even after checking my local Staples "Weekly Ad" Sales and applying my "Gift Card" I found that in most cases, I might as well just buy the item on Amazon. In fact, in some cases the prices were so bad that I would have actually saved money to throw my gift card in the garbage and just pay Amazon's full price (because Amazon's everyday price was more than $25 dollars less).

The good thing about a gift card is that the person who receives the card has 'mad money' that they can use to pick out whatever gift they want, the BAD thing is that if you give them a gift card to a store with LOUSY PRICES, then they may feel like their windfall gift money is being spent foolishly and feel bad (which pretty much sums up my feelings dealing with Staples).

Also, all my past experiences with Staples have seemed to involve that old-school bait-and-switch sales model where they dangle a sale item in your face, just to try to get you into the store, then RIP YOU OFF by telling you "So sorry, the sale item you want isn't available, but we do have a fine selection of our outrageously overpriced non-sale items, so wouldn't you rather have one of those instead?" Staples is not as bad as Best Buy (who are the worst scum in the universe in regard to bait-and-switch B.S.) but after buying on Amazon for the last few years, I am not ancious to play ANY of the brick an mortar store games of scampering around town like a rat in a maze trying to find that 'deal' before it disapears.

On Amazon, prices may change over time, but if an item is listed as available for a certain price, then you can buy it at the price shown, period, end of story."]

["These gift card holders are egg-cellent! (sorry) I was surprised by the size - it's as big as my face! You pull the egg from the top and bottom and it slides open with a "pop", displaying the gift card inside. The printing is professional and the magenta areas are actually shiny/glossy. It's made of thick, high quality card stock and should hold up to the tugging of almost any child - in fact, you could probably reuse it a number of times. There's plenty of space on the back to write a message, so there's no need to spend money on a separate greeting card. The card also has no branding, so you can replace the Amazon gift card with some other gift card if you wish. The cartoon chicken and the bright colors will appeal to young children, but it's also mature & simplistic enough to be appropriate for a teen or adult. I was very impressed by the quality of an item that is essentially free, and I definitely recommend this for an Easter present or any egg-related holiday.

The item came completely undamaged in a sealed plastic cover and was well protected during shipping, but YMMV. Sometimes Amazon's gift card tins arrive dented and scratched, and other times they're in perfect condition - it all depends on the person who packages and handles it."]

review_texts_seq:
["Here are a couple benefits to buying an Amazon gift card I don't think everybody thinks of. I read it before on some article about uses for Amazon gift cards and I think they are brilliant ideas.

Before I share my first one, let me start by saying that I don't remember how I lived to before Amazon and I don't want to try to remember it. It's kind of a similar feeling to when I think about how people must've lived before the Internet and how hard it must have been to have to go look things up at the library instead of googling them. So my first use for an Amazon gift card is actually just to build up a gift card amount to use to purchase my many many products that I am constantly making orders for on Amazon instead of using a credit card or debit card for each of those orders that early. The reason for that being that I ended up with line after line and page after page of Amazon orders on my credit card which made it really difficult to find any other purchases on there, most importantly possibly purchases that I did not make. My credit card has been stolen several times and the only way I found out was because I happened to see a purchase on The statement that was not familiar. Virtually impossible to do that now one almost everything says Amazon on my credit card bill. So instead I use an Amazon gift card to buy everything on Amazon and that leaves my credit card clear of Amazon plastered all over the statement.

The second thing that I use it for is actually just to get rid of other odds and ends of gift cards such as other visa gift cards and things like that that you get as a gift. I do that because usually End up with two dollars and change or so on on each of my leftover Visa gift cards and I have nothing to do with it because you can't spend it without knowing the exact balance and you have to remember that Number as you go to buy something andmake sure you're not applying to something that's more than what you have left on your card and it just turns into a huge pain. So instead of trying to use it from the visa gift card itself, I just buy an Amazon gift card with that which you can buy in any dollar amount and you can use a Visa gift card to purchase it, therefore getting rid of your visa gift card while using every single penny on it.

Those are my two biggest uses for Amazon gift cards and this hundred dollar gift card I got because Amazon was offering five dollars to you if you purchased $100 or more and Amazon gift cards, so why not? I know I probably spend that with in a month, if not a week :)"]

['I was really excited about the “anytime” gift card concept. I can keep a stack of gift cards ready for birthdays or last-minute gifts but pay for them and decide on the amount only when I need them!

Unfortunately, Amazon seems to have launched this product without testing it. What a nightmare the first time I tried to load one! I eventually figured out a way to do it, so let me save you the trouble:

You need to scan the QR code on the back of the gift card. As far as I can tell, Amazon hasn’t released any software that allows us to do this. You could type in the extremely long serial number manually, but the card is glued to the envelope right over the serial number, so revealing that requires you to remove the card from its gift envelope, thus ruining the gift envelope.

After many internet searches and three(!) third-party apps, here’s what worked for me:

Using my iPhone, I downloaded the free QR code reader named simply “Scan” from the App Store. Use that app to scan the QR code on the back of the gift card. (It’s very difficult to do because the code is so small and not centered in the window. Some apps won’t scan a code this small, but Scan has been working for me.)

The app will take you to an Amazon.com page and request your user name and password. Don’t enter this now! (I doubt it’s a good idea to put your Amazon password into ANY free, third-party app...)

Click the Safari icon in the lower right corner to open that page in your phone’s browser. Then log in to Amazon using your user name and password.

Finally, you should be taken to a page where you can load a balance onto your gift card. Amazon will probably make you re-enter your credit card information for “security purposes,” so have your card ready.

The good news is that so far, I haven’t experienced any of the problems that other reviewers mentioned where the recipient couldn’t use the card because the balance had been applied to the *purchaser’s* account! (Ugh!)

I hope Amazon fixes these problems soon, because the idea is great and I’d find many reasons to use these gift cards if it were easier!']

["The service does work as intended, however this evening has been has been a total unnecessary frustration because of this "reload" service.  Long story short, the past couple days I researched various parts for a new computer build and finally concluded my order summary.  The entire order was Prime eligible to have fast shipping, and I had been watching the Amazon purchase timer to make the indicated shipping date.  Then I found out that you can't use two cards to pay for your purchase, and perhaps this is well known for frequent Amazon shoppers, but I rarely order items these days.  After learning of this, I then spent the next 30 minutes looking at what options were available to get around this problem, and found at least three prominent suggestions between forums & videos. The most commonly suggested fix to this problem was to use the account "reload" option and within 5-10 minutes you could pay the specified partial amount towards the order using the loaded "Gift Card" balance.  Well two hours later it posts, and of coarse the shipping time is not eligible.  Given that I'm going to be working, I can't have an order as important at this delivered when no one is home.  UPS, Fedex, and USPS have all left packages sitting by the gates of my home, and of coarse things have been stolen (Multiple Houses) UPS is the only service which has noted the problem and now mandated their drivers to go to the actual door after I spoke up about to them.  I had arranged for someone to be home on delivery day which worked out well for them as well, but with the delay now in shipping it won't work.  I rarely ever complain about things, but this type of scenario should of been resolved years ago.  The solution should be clearly stated on the check out screen, and the alternative option convenient for the customer.  I mean seriously, when your the customer spending a large amount of money, you shouldn't have to go run around looking for solutions that may or may not work.  If I had known it would of taken 2 hours to use the balance, I would just done two orders, which has worked just fine in the past but requires more time to do but hell I would made the deadline.  Anyways I hope no one else makes my mistake.  Fry's Electronics had 80% of the items at the same price in store, with two items slightly cheaper, and 1 item $20 more.  If you have one or have something similar, it's can be worth while to just check them out.  The tax may be a little more which is what discouraged me, but you can use TWO payments, holy hell... out the door and back home for just a little more effort and $$.  Anyways, I just hope there is no more issues going forwards.  Don't get me wrong, I'm still gonna use Amazon in the future, but just for small stuff going forwards."]

Which is completely false and there is a department for verifying pending gift card transactions, but they will tell you there isn\'t and make you deal with them for multiple hours without helping you, and even their own customer service employees are not allowed to directly contact the department to verify your purchases.  And, if you miss any phone calls you are out of luck because there are no return calls received by these Amazon departments.  So my advice is to buy gift cards in person and then pay with it in checkout, but do not load it on your amazon account.  They also apparently have the authority to remove your gift card balance without any verification and you will not get the money back. Do not use this service.']

review_titles_seq: ["Please stop showing me $10 off $100 advertisements when I don't qualify.  Don't be evil."]
review_texts_seq:
['The rules for the $10 off $100 deal which is widely advertised include the provision that it is only good on the first time one has reloaded a gift card. I did that years ago before these advertisements started appearing, so I only qualify for $5 back on $100 which is the same as my amazon credit card so no benefit to me in going through the hassle of locking myself into the gift card reload.
In my more vulnerable mindstates, I have fallen for the "Oh, I\'ll just quickly reload my gift card before checking out to get the offer they are telling me is available". Only recently did I spend the 15 minutes of so that it took me to dig into the rules of the offer to realize that I was only getting 5% back.
And they make the process of getting $10 on $100 pretty opaque, with different payment options giving different rebates, IIRC splitting 10% up into two 5% credits at different times, which tends toward making someone who is only getting 5% back think they will get another 5% later on because that\'s what amazon said.
This is by far the most user-unfriendly user interface design I have seen on amazon, and feels like an indication that they have gained the monopoly power to stop being user-centered and start being evil.
Don\'t jump the shark amazon; stop showing the ad to people who don\'t qualify. And when people who don\'t qualify try to get the offer, be clear to them that they are not getting the offer.']

['Beware of signing up with ECA. They claim to represent the best interests of gamers, and that sounds great on paper, but they way they treat you when they get your credit card on file is far from being in your best interests.

The have continuously changed and edited their Terms of Service without asking members to re-accept the new terms, as most legitimate organizations will do (most organizations let you know the TOS has changed, not the ECA).

Their Terms of Service clearly states AT THIS TIME they will change the expiration date on your credit card if your card expires. They will change the expiration date until they get a "hit" to continue to charge you a fee.

If you try to simply cancel your credit card on file with them to stop them from charging you, their President has stated they will file fraud charges against you through your credit card company.

The only way to cancel your membership is by sending a snail mail letter. Yes, you can sign up on their website very easily, but have to send a letter in the mail to cancel. They also state they will not confirm receipt of your cancellation letter, meaning if it is "lost" in the mail, they will continue to charge you.

Their forums on their website have banned all new registrants the past few days without people even making one post. New registrations to their forums have also been shut down at this time.

When your first year of membership is up, they say they will inform you with 30 days left that your account membership will be auto-renwed for another $20, problem is, if you want to cancel, they have to receive your letter in the mail BEFORE the final 30 days. So when you get the notice that they are going to auto renew you for another year, it is already to late to cancel since you CANNOT cancel your membership on their website or by phone.

Finally, simply check out their Better Business Bureau rating. It states as I type this that "This business is not currently rated. BBB has recently received numerous complaints against this business, and will issue a rating after it has fully evaluated them."

review_texts_seq:
['When you get your gift card you are encouraged to register it on the website on the back of the card, in this case it was GiftCardMall. Very shortly after registering the card on the site it then showed the balance, ZERO. That registration site either has a dishonest employee taking information as forms are submitted or there could be malware on their server siphoning card information.

You can call the number on the back of the card to report the fraud and customer service (company: Blackhawk Network, who has poor reviews online) will tell you the name of the company that stole your funds, but you then have to fill out a dispute form and email it to them and then "in 7-10 days" (which has become over a month) they are supposed to give you a new card. A very inconvenient gift. For safety if you get one of these cards use it up immediately or better yet move it to your Amazon gift card balance for safe keeping.

UPDATE: almost 5 weeks has gone by and the issue is has still not been resolved by the gift card company (Blackhawk Network). After several long annoying calls to them they say that Covid has slowed down their responses. And they acknowledged there is theft happening on their registration sites, how it is allowed to continue without being fixed is mind boggling. Every couple weeks they will send out an email asking for copies of the same documents (proof of purchase) even if you already sent them in several times prior. This is a complete failure of customer service.

Suggestion: Rethink this stressful risky "gift", find a different gift card company that is more reliable for customer service. Your safest bet is an Amazon gift card since they have the best customer service teams.']

review_titles_seq: ['Two $100 Gift Cards were Empty, but Customer Service was Great']
review_texts_seq:
["I normally order the e-mail Amazon gift codes, which I've never had a problem with, but when my wife and I wanted to give an end of the school year gift to my sons' teachers, I ordered two $100 gift cards so she could give them to the teachers on the last day of school. They were surprised and thrilled to receive them.

Well, fast forward to the first week of the new school year. The teachers from last year, embarassed to have to approach my wife about it, told her that the gift cards were EMPTY and didn't work. Humiliating for us as parents after having thought we did a good deed.

We were worried about getting a refund or replacement because of three months that had passed while school was out for the summer. I used Amazon chat support, and was pleasantly surprised that they offered to refund the amounts with no hassles. We didn't even have to recite back the codes or send the cards back (we had asked for them back from the teachers for this purpose)

Conclusion: Think twice about ordering these, and consider the Amazon E-Codes as a better option. 1 star for complete product failure, and 5 stars for great customer support, averaged out and rounded up gives this transaction three stars."]

So there was no waiting until Christmas to find out what was inside the pretty white box with the purple ribbon (or ordering these to put on/under the Christmas tree as gift teasers). Total fail on Amazons part.

If the box didn\'t have the clear plastic part on the bottom I would have been more surprised at least but then the invoice sheet gave it away when I pulled out the personalized message inside the mailing envelope. If you order this for someone as a gift and don\'t want them to have it right away send it to someone else first or let the recipient know not to open the package coming in the mail. The box is nice from the top and the presentation is nice, just mailing as a gift option doesn\'t work out too well.']

["I buy these cards all the time. They help me with spending issues I've had in the past.  They work wonderfully. However, based on a lot of the reviews I've read, it's important you read the info pamphlet so you clearly understand how to go about using it.  This will avoid many of the frustrations I read about in other reviews.  First, this card can not be used to retrieve cash.  Second, if you plan on using it for online purchases you need to register it in your name which will link it to your zip code. When merchants run CC #'s, the 4 main things that need to match with the card are name, card #, zip code and most of the time the CVV # on the back of the card. As long as you registered it correctly any online purchase will always go through assuming there's enough $ on the card.  Third, every retailers CC machines operate differently. So, it's important to ask the cashier if their machine automatically subtracts the amount available on the card from your purchase balance or if you need to tell them the exact amount that's on the card so they can manually punch that in before you swipe the card.  Asking this will avoid the card from getting declined. If your purchase balance is less then what's available on the card, then you don't need to ask. Also, there's been a handful of times where mine got declined even though I knew I had plenty of funds. I just re-ran the card as debit instead of credit and it works.  If you haven't registered your card and need to run it as debit, the pin is the last 4 digits on the card.  Fourth, if you purchase items that may hv a chance of being returned, try very hard to keep that card on hand even if it's all used up.  Most retailers insist they reimburse your $ bk onto its original form of payment or you'll end up with store credit. There's been many times I went to return and threw out my card already and had to basically make a scene to get cash back.  Lastly, never ever ever pay at the pump when getting gas w these types of prepaid cards.  There's extra security set up on the CC machine at gas pumps. It knows its a prepaid card, so it will hold all the funds available on your card for probably 7 days. Any retailer that accepts CC has to batch out their machine before any of those funds are deposited into their bank account. This is why they hold the funds.  And honestly for whatever reason that I don't understand it seems that these cards can't be used to pay bills online or over the phone. But, that's no fault of the card. That will happen no matter what prepaid card you use.  I hope this helps as you scroll along other reviews regarding their troubles they experienced. I believe if you are aware of this then it will help avoid any frustrations and help you determine if this is the right type of card depending on your needs."]

['More than anything else, convenience is what Amazon sells to the world. So convenience is what we expect and grow accustomed to. When Amazon is not convenient it is extremely frustrating.

So my son had a couple of $100.00 visa gift cards and really wanted to purchase an IPOD. I tried using them to help make the purchase, but once I entered one of the cards to make the purchase, it took my order without telling me to enter another source for additional funds. Realizing that Amazon would have to cancel the transaction because it only allowed for one payment source, I cancelled the transaction and tried to enter the Visa gift cards onto an Amazon.com gift card so that I could then add them together to make the purchase.

So I first added the amount over $200.00 that I would need to make the purchase to my Amazon.com gift card then and tried to enter the Visa gift cards. Amazon would not accept the gift cards. Since I already had the extra money on an Amazon.com gift card, I decided to "buy" my son\'s visa gift cards to use elsewhere and put $200.00 onto Amazon.com gift card from my own funds. The transaction appeared as pending for hours. After a while, I gave up waiting and just paid for my son\'s purchase. Now I have $200.00 on an Amazon.com gift card that I will likely eventually use, but never really wanted there in the first place.

I suppose there is a way to reverse the charge, but everything related to the Amazon.com gift seems to be so complicated, I just don\'t want to take the time and hassle to do it. I probably don\'t even have the time to write this review, but I am so annoyed by how long it took to accomplish this transaction.

If Amazon is going to continue to make a run on leading the retail world, it will have to figure out how people can make purchases with visa gift cards. It will also have to figure out how to reload balances without making customers wait hours. If it continues to be this complicated, some other retailer will figure out how to do it, and shoppers will go elsewhere.']

review_texts_seq: ['This Reload works fine throughout Amazon online store. Amazon Reload is what Amazon Gift/e-gift card is except Reload works only with your account. However, Amazon.com Store card, which is a physical card can be used with Amazon Pay, AWS, and the rest of Amazon. Not to be confused with Amazon Rewards Visa Signature Card, which is provided by Chase, and can be used with everything I believe. Another type of physical cards are the Amazon Classic gift card, which you can find at other stores, which are the same as eGift card/Reload. Some of the cards I mentioned offer cashbacks, and do not include Amazon Business American Express cards which you might have guessed is for businesses. But a customer without a  business can acquire them too for their "business needs," as stated by their FAQ, as if the other non-business cards are meant for non-business needs. ["I'm a Mac person but Microsoft really got me with Office 365. At first I was annoyed to have a subscription service but since I'm part of a family of 5, it worked out that we got our money's worth. Office isn't a perfect application--I LOVE Excel more than Numbers and Word is more complete than Pages but can t clunkier, not organized as well, and not as good for Desktop publishing and images. But Office at this price is excellent.
The next thing I hated was that 365 switched from the number of devices to the number of users. I could STAND that my home computer that my 3 kids used had to have separate logins for applications on the same computer. BUT, when Dropbox continually refused to offer smaller monthly packages and limited the number of devices on their free version, I started to look elsewhere. Lo and behold Microsoft OneDrive was my answer. And it was ALREADY INCLUDED with my Office 365. Now everyone in my family has 1 TB of OneDrive storage and they can access it on their iphones, laptops or wherever they can get an internet connection. I can share REALLY LARGE VIDEO FILES with as many parents from the school that I want. I can share lots of school videos for the parents to download AND I don't have to store them on my computer. In other words I can have them on the cloud (OneDrive) and they don't have to sync to my computer. This frees up a lot of space on my computer. (I save copies on external drives of course.) Good-bye Dropbox!
So this has become an essential part of my life and one of the subscription services I consider a must-have along with Amazon Prime."]

review_titles_seq: ['Holiday Gift Cards In Great Snowflake Tins, Love These!']
review_texts_seq:
["UPDATE 12/7/13: If you're thinking of ordering these for the 2013 holidays don't wait until the last minute. Last year the $50 denomination was sold out by mid December and they didn't get any more until after the holidays.

These are nice looking holiday gift cards with great, versatile snowflake boxes. The boxes are NOT cardboard. They are tins(metal containers) which look very nice and open and close well. They are a good quality. Although they have a snowflake design, they are attractive enough to be repurposed into things like containers to hold earrings or other small items after the holidays.

When I placed my order I was a bit worried because the order said [Paper Gift Certificate], but the gift cards I received are regular plastic cards like credit cards.

I bought one $50 Amazon gift card with snowflake tin that I am giving for the holidays. But I also plan on giving a lot of other types of gift cards for Xmas and most don't come with any kind of box or container which means you have to buy a little box for about $1.99 or find a card to put them in to make them presentable gifts.

So I spent an additional $200 to get 4 extra snowflake tins to use for the holidays for other gift cards. I have young nieces who will just love these containers. And now that I have a $200 Amazon Gift Card Balance I'm using it to pick up other holiday gifts on Amazon. Win-Win for me as the tins are basically free since I shop a lot on Amazon. Plus I paid for it with my Amazon.com Rewards Visa so I'm pretty sure I'll earn 3 points per $1 spent.(I don't think there is any exclusion for gift cards. Should find out in a few days.)

With the Free One-Day Shipping I was able to order these on Dec 9th and received them on Dec 10th. They were securely packaged stacked inside a cardboard wrap around mailer. I would have preferred them to ship in a regular box with each one individually bubble wrapped, but none of mine were damaged.

Originally Amazon was only offering these gift cards in denominations of $50 (they got a bunch of low ratings because people wanted more denominations), but more choices have been added. Choose from $50, $75, $100, $150, $200, $250, $350, $500, $750 & $1000.

UPDATE 12/18/12: I guess these have become quite popular, the $50 denomination is sold out."]

["This is serious. I did not order the “Amazon Reload”, but my account was charged $100 from my credit card on Dec 2. I do not and never have had an Amazon Gift Card). Amazon loaded someone else’s card or account. I called Amazon immediately and was sent to the Fraud Department, where I explained. They said to change my password and they would investigate. They believed that it was sent to another’s card or gift certificate, but I never received a follow-up and my account was never reimbursed. My Amazon Order page doesn’t show any dispute or status and there is no way to dispute the charge on the Amazon Reload Order page or halt or reverse the Reload the payment.
My Amazon account was apparently hacked. I called Norton the same day and they removed malware from my PC. I reported it to my credit card company to dispute the claim, but have not heard back. They advised me to change my credit card. No indication from Amazon that I will be reimbursed. Now I received an Amazon Email asking me to rate the transaction, which shows the left hand doesn’t know what the right hand is doing. I will not buy an Amazon Gift Card, nor trust their system, if they do not take steps to remedy the situation and prevent it from happening again to myself or others. By making it easy to Reload a card, they made it easy to hack. I would rate it no stars, but the system won't allow it."]

['I am a long time prime member with Amazon.  I do almost all of my Holiday shopping and the greater part of my regular shopping through Amazon.  Last month I received a email gift card from my brother for my birthday. When I attempted to apply the gift card to my account, Amazon advised me that it had already been redeemed.  I reviewed all my recent purchases and confirmed that I had not redeemed the card.  I attempted to resolve the issue with Amazon but was told that I needed to have the purchaser contact Amazon to resolve the issue.  They would not tell me who or how the gift card was spent.  My brother argued with Amazon for three days in order to resolve the problem and was ultimately told that he would have to dispute the purchase through his bank.  They told him that they could not confirm who spent the gift card or what purchases were made.  Both my brother and I are beyond upset.  Amazon is a HUGE company who certainly has the resources to resolve the problem with better customer service.  Lesson learned - we won\'t ever buy a gift card from them again.  Ultimately Amazon is the one who will miss out. 2nd try was also rejected. These aren't instant rejections.... they are card denied rejections that happen 5-10 minutes after the order happens. Again no reason as to why this happened.

Called customer service. The advice there wasn't helpful and they didn't really know what was going on. What I eventually figured out was that each time I put an order in, it was charging a $1 authorisation fee to the card. Then the card has a $99 balance instead of $100 and the transaction is rejected. Probably not news to most people but its not common knowledge, after all Amazon Customer Service didn't know what was up..."]

['I received this item today and boy, was I pleasantly surprised! What an elegant looking tin. It\'s a lovely presentation for a gift card. It\'s bigger than I thought it would be at "5-1/8" X "3/8". It\'s a stocking stuffer for my husband but I suspect we will probably hold onto it afterward and use it to give another gift card to someone next year. It\'s that nice.

That said, there are some things I should clarify, one being the free shipping. Amazon advertizes free one day shipping but when you place the order the confirmation says free two day shipping. This didn\'t matter to me. Hopefully, I am never in a position where it will. I ordered the afternoon of Dec. 17th, and it was at my door in 48 hours. Impressive. I am not complaining about getting a free gift tin and free expedient shipping, I simply want to point it out. It\'s somewhat confusing and deceptive.

The other point I wanted to make was about a message you can include with your order. Don\'t bother. It\'s simply a note written on the packing slip. If you need to address the gift or feel compelled to jot something down, might I suggest adhering a gift tag to the underside of the tin. Why do they have slots cut out of the bottom of the tin? I suspect it has something to do with being able to scan the card\'s bar code. Anyway, if you need to put a tag on it that\'s where I would do it.

I considered rating this item only 4 stars because of these two issues, but I truly feel that the item is still worthy of the high marks and the issues are too small to demerit.

Thank you, Amazon!

Merry Christmas']

['As a long time Amazon.com customer, a gift card seemed like a good purchase. I am just trying to purchase a card to have e-mailed. I basically wanted to convert a Visa debit gift card into an Amazon.com gift card. I put the amount of the card in, the number and expiration date. Amazon accepted it as payment, but after hours of not receiving a confirmation e-mail I checked the site to see what was going on. The site claimed they could not confirm the payment, yet they had already taken money off the Visa gift card. I contacted customer service who told me a Visa gift card is not the best way to purchase an Amazon gift card and they would refund the money to the Visa gift card. I then put in another order using my Amazon.com credit card. A card I have used thousands of times before and never had a problem. This time, I received the same message I got when using the Visa gift card. I contacted Customer Service again. The first person I spoke to told me I had a "Block" on the account. She could not tell me why that was there, and she informed me she could remove it immediately. This claim brought me some concern so I asked to speak with her manager to find out the reason  a "Block" had been placed. The manager claimed there was no "Block" on the card and the sale should have gone through fine. So, I again went back and checked on the sale. Again there was a message that it could not be paid using the payment option I had selected. I called back again and told them to cancel the sale. This is extremely disappointing to me, as I have felt for quite some time that Amazon was one of the last customer service oriented sellers around. I guess they too have been pushed to the "Make money, screw the customer" attitude this country has been forced into with our economic situation. A trusted company has gone down the drains. I hope to see you come back to your original ideals some day Amazon.']

The way I use it for multiple cards is to reload from one card, then another until I have distributed the funding sources. It literally takes seconds per reload, and when I am using three or more cards, it can all be done in a minute or two. Then when I need to make a purchase the entire amount is waiting. This is much faster and more efficient than purchasing multiple gift cards.

["I purchase Amazon Gift cards every year during Christmas and they always arrive promptly and attractively packaged.  This year, however, something happened and I received two boxes of gift cards on the same day, duplicate orders.  I assumed that there was a processing glitch at Amazon and that only one of the orders of cards was valid.  I received no communication from Amazon conveying which order was the good order, and couldn't determine which was the good order without activating the cards myself (and this wouldn't work, as they aren't transferable after activation).  So I took a chance and gave out a set from one of the boxes and held onto the other set just in case.  As my luck would have it, when my nephews and nieces tried to use the cards, they didn't work.  The gift cards I gave out were the invalid ones.  Fortunately, my nephews and nieces are good kids and they knew I would make it right.  So, through the help of my sister-in-law and a lot of time texting, we got the good card information to the kids.  Even though it all worked out in the wash, Amazon certainly could have made it a lot easier with one little email.  I'll definitely have to reassess my gift card purchases next year."]

review_texts_seq: ["Two years ago I bought a $50 gift certificate to give my sister.  I figured on Amazon she could find something that she'd like and I would not make a bad purchase thus disappointing her.  My sister didn't have an Amazon account so had to open one before she tried to purchase something. When I tried to apply the code to my account, I discovered it was already used.  I ended up having to use my sister's account to make a purchase for myself with the $50 gift certificate.  When you apply a gift certificate (even if you don't even use it because your order was not successful!) the gift certificate amount is *fixed* to your account. Troublesome."]

The process of using Amazon Reload is incredibly simple and efficient. By linking my bank account to my Amazon account, I can easily add funds with just a few clicks. The best part is that I no longer need to enter my debit or credit card information for every purchase, eliminating the hassle of manually inputting sensitive details each time. This not only saves me time but also ensures a secure shopping experience.

What sets Amazon Reload apart from other payment methods is the added benefit of earning a reload reward. Every time I reload my Amazon account with $100 or more, I receive a 2% cashback reward in the form of Amazon credits. This bonus incentive has proven to be a pleasant surprise, as it allows me to stretch my shopping budget even further. Whether it's purchasing household essentials, electronics, or even treating myself to a well-deserved indulgence, the extra credits from Reload provide a welcome boost to my purchasing power.

Overall, Amazon Reload has become an indispensable tool in my online shopping arsenal. Its user-friendly interface, seamless integration with my bank account, and the added reward system make it a top choice for managing my Amazon spending. If you're an avid Amazon shopper looking to simplify your payment process and enjoy the benefits of cashback rewards, I highly recommend giving Amazon Reload a try"]

review_texts_seq:
['I purchased this card as a birthday gift. The recipient tried to use the card in a Subway store, but was told it had to be activated first -- quite embarrassing for him and for me. But neither he nor I had received an activation code. In fact, he said the card arrived with a message that it was "ACTIVE" in bold lettering.

After contacting GiftCardMall and speaking with someone who had limited English comprehension, he was told he would have to get the activation code from me. I called them myself to explain I had never received an activation code. This rep also barely spoke English, and after I had explained the problem in detail, he actually asked me to give him the activation code. (?!) Um...that\'s the point here. He finally promised someone would contact me within 1 business day. When that didn\'t happen, I called again, and was told same thing. No one ever called.

I tried e-mailing instead, and received a notice that someone would reply within 1-2 business days. Four days later, I still hadn\'t heard from anyone. Despite 4 phone calls and 2 e-mails to GiftCardMall, they never resolved the issue, or even bothered to call me back to tell me they couldn\'t resolve it.

After a week of waiting and no response whatsoever, I finally insisted on speaking with a supervisor, who issued the first apology I had received for the problem but asked me to be "patient". Yeah, right. All this trouble and waiting for such a simple, basic problem. I insisted on a refund if they couldn\'t resolve the problem that day -- not the same old "1 to 2 business days" later routine...again. Several hours later I received a refund notice. Finally, at last, a response.

GiftCardMall clearly has some serious problems in the customer service department -- not the least of which are language barriers. Their reps could sorely use some intensive customer service training and lessons on follow-through.']

review_texts_seq:
["To be honest this is the most insecure function of Amazon or any other online store that I have ever seen, and I have never even used it personally.

This is the THIRD time that I have had to report fraudulent purchases on my account to Amazon support that were made through their online gift card feature. The first time it was $300 and the two more recent ones were $100 each. Every time I have had to report the breach and have Amazon or my bank refund the purchase and reset the account.

I have two factor authentication turned on, have changed my password multiple times and during this most recent breach even I did not have access to the account. After the second breach I had Amazon temporarily disable the account and reset the password randomly, so that even I didn't know what the password was. And STILL someone managed somehow to access the account and charge money to the online gift card.

Honestly at this point I am getting frustrated enough to just stop using Amazon completely and destroy my account. And I know for a fact that my computer and my phon AND my email have not all three been hacked at the same time. The two factor authentication on my phone isn't even connected to the internet. It's a randomly generated code that is changed every few seconds, so the only way to even get the code is to have access to my phone itself.

There has to be some kind of back door that someone is using to get to the account and reload the gift card balance. And it's only the gift card that seems to be the issue because they aren't making purchases directly with the card on file. Whatever this issue is Amazon needs to resolve it ASAP, as it is a major security issue."]

review_texts_seq:
["I don't know what kind of sweatshop these guys are running, but I've had problems with them since day ONE--I tried to give them ZERO STARS, but I HAD to give them at least one (which is being generous, in my opinion). I ordered my cards well in advance, and they still did not arrive on time. When I called the company to figure out what the issue was, they sent my phone call to somewhere in India--I was put on hold numerous times while they scrambled around trying to figure out what was going on with an order they had sent. When they finally had some information, they GUARANTEED a delivery date--the date passed with NO cards in the mail whatsoever. Apparently, this 'company' (and I use that term very loosely) takes 2+ weeks to process and send out FAULTY orders.

When the individual DID receive the card it looked as though it had been used, and did not even WORK. When I explained to 'GiftCard Mall' what had happened, and told them that my mother said it looked like the card was in rough condition (the individual at the store the card was purchased for, in fact, confirmed the card HAD been reloaded--she had guessed it was multiple times from the shape the card was in), they implied that she was lying about it! review_titles_seq: ['A gift card... what could go wrong? Here’s what did and how Amazon fixed it...']
review_texts_seq:
['It’s a reloaded gift card. What could possibly go wrong?

Actually, I did have something go wrong.

On Black Friday, I got an offer for an extra $10 to refill a gift cart for $100. That’s 10% free... I’ll definitely take that deal.

I clicked the link which took me to the checkout, and I wondered why I didn’t see the $10 bonus anywhere. I went ahead anyway and checked out.

I got the $100, but not the $10. I was pretty bummed, but I had no way to prove that I’d clicked on the $10 bonus link.

About a week later, I got irritated enough to actually reach out to customer service via the in-app chat.

To my surprise, CS acknowledged the mistake and credited me the $10. The catch was that it’d be applied at my next purchase. Again, it was not visible to me (afaik).

It was successfully applied on my next purchase, so everything worked out correctly in the end

I have always trusted Amazon to do the right thing, but this time I had no evidence to prove what I’d done. The fact that they honored their offer earned deep trust from me.

I’m a happy customer (again).']

review_titles_seq: ['... many of the reviews here in an attempt to better understand how Spa Finder works']
review_texts_seq: ["I read many of the reviews here in an attempt to better understand how Spa Finder works. I did this because when trying to redeem my Spa Finder gift cards that my mom sent me for my birthday, my spa did not have a clear policy on what I could use them for and gave me a confusing explanation of how I could not use the gift card for discounted packages because I had received a discount when purchasing the gift card. First, my mom paid full price for the gift cards, so there was no discount. I had a long conversation with the owner and did some of my own research. What I learned is that Spa Finder makes money by charging a commission to the spa on the redemption of cards. In essence, Spa Finder only reimburses the spa for a percentage of the card. There is no discount to the client in purchasing the card, so spas should be aware that just because Spa Finder does not reimburse them in full for the gift cards does not mean that client received a discount (it's not a coupon or a voucher). Many of the reviews have advised to either just give the person money or a gift card directly from the spa to avoid these hassles. I have a different take on this. My mom lives across the country and she gave me these gift cards because it is more personal than sending a check or cash, and it ensures that I will use it for its intended purpose.She could not buy a card directly from the spa because of her location. Whatever you think of Spa Finder as a company, spas choose to participate in the Spa Finder program as a way of building their clientele. It is a legitimate business decision, and the price is the monthly fee the spas pay as well as the commissions on each card that is redeemed at their location. While the fees may be higher, this is a similar concept to the charges that credit card companies place on each transaction. Regardless of the transaction charges, business accept credit cards as convenience to customers so they can build their customer base. Similarly, spas participate in the Spa Finder program to build their clientele. The Spa Finder program is not mandatory, and spas know about the charges before they sign up. I do not feel sorry for spas that choose to participate in this program, so talk of "supporting" your local spa falls on deaf ears with me. A spa is not a charity that needs my support. It is a business just like any other, and I expect the spas listed on the website to accept the cards as payment. If the cost of participating in the Spa Finder program outweighs the benefits, they should not participate. Similarly, it they no longer wish to participate, they should remove their name from the Spa Finder website and place a notice on their own website that they no longer participate in the program. Spas should really think about how participating in the program will affect their business rather than leaving it up to the client to wade through the technicalities. I recommended to the owner of my spa that they add a section to their policy page explaining that because of the commissions they pay on the Spa Finder cards, clients can redeem the cards only for full-priced services and cannot apply the cards to discounted packages. Spas can develop any policy that serves their business best, but whatever the policy, it should be clearly stated to the client upfront. I gave this three stars because that means that its OK. Not great, not bad, but OK. I think it could be great, but there are obviously some things to be worked out on Spa Finder's part (based on other reviews) as well as that of businesses participating in the program. Right now, the potential loser in this situation is the client."]

review_texts_seq:
["I actually am a huge fan of Amazon Gift Card and also of the "Balance Reload." In the last 6 months I've been making a lot more purchases on Amazon than I did before (for a variety of reasons) and there are two things that I've noticed that kind of bothered me: A.) When looking at my credit card statement it always just says the amount, and that it was purchased via Amazon, so there are a ton of entries for Amazon purchases that don't really mean anything to me. B.) it's really easy to spend a lot of money because, well. . . you can find pretty much anything on Amazon and it's too easy to buy with things like 1-click purchasing, subscribe and save, etc.
Reloading a gift card balance means that I still get my rewards points for buying things on Amazon, but can also very easily set a budget for myself beforehand. Also, every-time that I buy something I'll be able to see how much I have left of that original amount. In short, if you buy a lot of things off of Amazon I would highly recommend using this feature. I still have some things that I buy through 1-click purchasing . . . but most everything else I use gift cards for."]

review_texts_seq:
['I have five daughters. They have asked for gift cards in the past. For specific places and/or the Visa ones. I used to buy them at the store for $10 and $15, just for specific places, for friends’ birthdays, etc.

Why did I wait so long?! Lol! I guess I felt that gift cards were initially ‘cold’ and impersonal, and from someone who just didn’t want to bother shopping for that person. But that’s not really true. At least not now. My girls understand I want them to know I care about them and chose things that they would like or that they specifically asked for.

They let me know they are getting older, and can choose a lot of things for themselves. Plus, it gives them a little bit of freedom to make their own purchases! I am totally good with that, and buying them through. Amazon was SO EASY (even for this nearly 60 year old mom!) and made me confident and comfortable that there wouldn’t be any problems. And there have not been! Very happy! 5⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️']

review_texts_seq: ['As I was making a purchase thru Amazon, I was offered additional $5.00 to my gift card if I placed an order for $100.00 to my gift card balance and my remaining balance owed would be $107.00 on an item costing $112.00.  I had never done this and was not aware of how it worked.  I followed the blue links to read about it because I wanted to use all of my remaining gift card balance to make my purchase, not just the $5.00 being offered.  I read the reviews.  One review stated you can only use your gift card balance to make purchases.  Another stated they never received their additional $5.00 credit after reloading their gift card.  I went ahead and reloaded $100.00 on my gift card, and immediately received email that $100.00 was added to my gift card balance.  I was expecting it to say $105.00 was being added.  I went ahead and purchased my $112.00 item in full with my gift card balance and immediately received email notice that my additional $5.00 credit had been applied to my gift card balance.  I made another purchase today for another item on Amazon with the intention to use reward points on one of my credit cards already on file as one of my payment methods.  When I placed the order, the payment method had defaulted to use the remaining balance on my gift card balance.  I selected the blue link to change payment method to use my reward points on my credit card with any remaining balance to be paid with my credit card and removed the black dot on the radial button for my gift card balance by clicking on it and was able to save the remaining of my gift card balance with this purchase.  I reviewed everything in my order to make sure it was correct before submitting it.  I am giving a 4 star review because the system had defaulted to encourage me to use my gift card balance using $5.00 with my first order and I wanted to pay in full with my gift card balance since I had just made purchase of $100.00 to reload it and also because the second purchase I made defaulted to pay with my remaining gift card balance. ['Word to the wise! Amazon will charge other payment forms without your explicit consent or even notification of your original payment fails. TURN OFF THAT SETTING IF YOU WANT TO AVOID A HEADACHE. (Account, payment preferences, scroll all the way to the bottom and click “backup payment preferences,” toggle option off). We didn’t realize Amazon charged other cards instead of loading those visa gift cards to the balance.

Here’s the quick and dirty:
-I had one of those visa gift cards from a rebate.
-I had a purchase I washed to make on Amazon.
-The purchase was for more than my visa gift card.
-Amazon doesn’t allow you to specify multiple forms of payment at checkout.
-I “loaded” my visa gift card to my amazon balance.
-I received an e-mail three days later showing my $50 was added.
-I made my purchase.
-Weeks later, I noticed a $50 charge on a different credit card. I called, was told to dispute the charge with my credit card company. It was ultimately denied. So, that visa rebate gift card was never loaded to the account.
-Some time later, we learned that there’s a place where you can turn off a setting, one that I was never told about, that will charge another card of your first payment method doesn’t process.']

On August 14 attempted to use card at CVS cashier for $8.36 purchase. Advised only $0.01 available.

Contacted gift card company and they sent email showing fraudulent transactions. My dad completed forms and sent back. Dad just contacted me asking for purchase receipt.

All of this was a major hassle and turned out to be a terrible gift.

Bottom line. Gift card company sells $100 card. Waits for activation. Then after complaint, they provide this type email showing multiple transactions that are not realistic but amounts to $99.99. They then require extensive paperwork and phone information (name, address, phone) and indicate it will be 60-90 days for them to investigate with retail merchants on the transactions. review_texts_seq:
['Ummm... they are gift cards. They operated according to my expectations... just like any other gift card.', 'I use apple devices all the time, but I wasn\'t overly familiar with Apple gift cards. I typed in "Apple store gift cards" into Amazon, and it showed me this. I bought it as a gift. It turns out the person wanted "Apple store gift cards" (as I typed in), but these are "Apple App Store & iTunes gift cards). I didn\'t realize there was a difference. I figured it\'s the same company, how could there be two separate ones? Surely they are interchangeable or convertible. WRONG! They definitely CANNOT be used interchangeably. I contacted support to see if I could do something to fix this (I read in forums of people converting them over via Apple support). So I did all the stuff the support site said to do, submitted the request. Then they got back to me and said since I bought them from Amazon, not directly from Apple, there was no way for them to convert them over for me. So I\'m stuck with $250 dollars of app store and itunes credit and the person I bought these for (and myself) rarely ever buy anything from that. So yay! Flushing money down the toilet! And for reference, you CAN use xbox and microsoft store gift cards interchangeably. And no, I\'m not an xbox/ms fanboy. I like apple devices, but this situation is bs.

If you want to avoid all this bs, read up on the difference between apple store and apple app store gift cards and buy them directly from Apple or don\'t buy them at all. Don\'t buy them on Amazon because it limits your recourse if something goes wrong as I learned the hard way.

I consider myself pretty knowledge on most digital matters, but I failed on this one. I pity the poor grandparent or other less-knowledgeable individual that has to deal with this. Two thumbs down.']
