review_titles_seq: ['New Amazon Gift Card reloading process: unexpected & time consuming.']
review_texts_seq:
['The previous system was very clear and easy to use. Reloading one’s Gift Card was quick and the funds were available immediately. There was no announcement or explanation for this change… a change that does not appear to make things any easier or better for the Amazon customer.

Now, it appears we have to purchase a gift card from ACI Gift Cards, Inc. and then this Gift Card is supposed to automatically be applied to our Amazon Gift card balance in about 5 minutes… with the caveat that it may take longer.

I started maintaining a Gift Card balance because I use Virtual Credit Cards for internet purchases. Virtual Credit Cards can only be used at one merchant. Unfortunately, Amazon can charge any given item to any one of 5 (or more) different merchants with little or no information about which merchant will be charged at the time of purchase. This means that orders with multiple items could have some item purchases rejected due to payment issues. Fixing this can delay the order process for days. Reloading the Gift Card using a Virtual Credit Card is a way to get around this problem. The only real downside is having to maintain a balance with Amazon that can only be used at Amazon.']

["I ordered a $100 gift card for a friend's wedding gift. It was a destination wedding and I wasn't attending in person but based on the expected delivery date it should have arrived before she left so I was ok with that. I just found out after chatting with her a month later that she never received the gift. She contacted amazon as it was on her registry as purchased and was transferred a couple of times. As the purchaser, I contacted amazon to request a refund and have them re-issue a card and expedite shipping. They said sure, just go ahead and order the new one and I will refund your account right after. That made no sense to me but I was going to do it until going through the process I realized I needed to change the shipping address. Now I'm really angry because I have to look up the darn address again. Seconds later I was told, I can't issue the refund because it has to go through the gift card blah blah blah department and I would get a call back on Monday. At this point I'm irate and asked to speak to a supervisor. After a long hold I was told the supervisor approved a refund now but I can still go ahead and reorder. My response is that I'm not reordering anything until I get evidence that a refund is going to my credit card. This was an awful experience and I don't trust ordering gift cards from amazon again. I don't know what carrier was used but whatever disconnect happened between the shipping of the gift-card and the delivery is not my problem. I'm also disappointed that Amazon has no controls in place that would show an order has been in transit for so long. I should have noticed as well but I'm the customer and I want my ordering experience to be seamless.

Update:4/29 - my friend told me that someone drove to her home in their personal vehicle and hand delivered the gift card to her on Sunday which was the day after I complained. That was a good move but I'm still very disappointed in this service."]

review_titles_seq: ['Annoyed with my denomination not being available.']
review_texts_seq:
["Unaccustomed to giving gift cards, I happened to spot this advertised. Though I did not like all the negative reviews about the packaging, I figured it was an in house gift so decided to continue pursuit. Wanting to order a $100 version, I only saw versions to click on for $50 and $150. Upon clicking on the $50, planning to order two, I saw that you could select other denominations. As customary with my purchasing habits, I like to think things over a bit, so decided to have my breakfast and return. After deciding to go ahead with the order, I went back to the gift card page, and selected this particular boxed display, and the denominations began at $150. I made other attempts for about 10 minutes, all failing to provide the $100 option, and found the $50 links still led to the $150 minimum. Next I tried to find how I could call Amazon and speak to a live person or a live chat, and though they do not make the process easy to find or execute, I did find I could provide them with my phone number and they would call me back. That happened pretty quickly, but the voice connection was poor, and the operator that called was not exactly a genius. It took forever for her to determine exactly what I was getting at, and eventually it took me about 5 minutes to provide her with the item's ID number and confirm its' accuracy through repeated dialog. Finally it turned out she could not find a way for me to purchase a $100 denomination, and proceeded to suggest how I could purchase other denominations at $150 and above or I could purchase one of the many other options they have. She did agree and comment on how nice the Santa display was, but insisted on suggesting other alternatives. I declined other suggestions, and convinced her I had other local options that I could pick up with a short, local drive.

It still puzzles me how they could not provide that denomination at 10 am but not 11 am, but still provide other denominations. The free one day shipping is for today only, so I will check back later and see if they have fixed the problem or at least note a problem with lower denominations. Annoyed!!!"]

review_titles_seq: ['There is Zero Reason to Dislike This Or To Pay WIth Another Method']
review_texts_seq:
["I never just buy things with my debit/credit cards directly. Amazon gives you 2% more purchasing power if you use a debit card and have linked your checking account to your Amazon account, and then use that card to reload with. Literally- LITERALLY- they are giving you $2 per $100 for FREE. The process is also as straight-forward and streamlined as one could realistically demand (I guess it'd be better if it sensed when and how much I wanted to load telepathically and then immediately did it, but only slightly).

For some, this route will help them conserve money and foster/impose financial self-discipline. You can designate only so much to spend per month on Amazon, and see at a glance how much you have left. (Of course, the ease with which you can add more if you want to go over budget undermines this potential purpose if you already completely lack self-discipline.). If you have a household member, you could give them an allowance of sorts via this method, too, I reckon.

But the sole reason I pay with my Amazon Gift Card 100% of the time is the 2% boost to my purchasing power. When you're poor (even when you're not: why'd you not take a 2% boost that is so trivally easy even if you were Trump or Bezos?), these sorts of bonuses can be more impactful than the low % might seem upon perfunctory reflection. The discounted Prime for being low-income is also nice. Thanks, Amazon! (that said, stop being a jerk about paying taxes and employees- everyone else matters, too)"]

['Obviously, getting a gift card is awesome. And I hate to be one to look a gift horse in the mouth. However, what\'s the deal with only being able to use an Amazon.com Gift Card on Amazon.com? Why not Amazon.co.uk?

This may sound nit-picky, but consider this- just after Christmas, on Amazon.co.uk there was a sale- the "Twelve Days of Kindle" sale. Loads of Kindle Books for real cheap. I got excited, browsed through, chose which ones I was going to use my gift card on, and was set to check out. Looking at the check out page, though, I realized I wasn\'t going to be able to use the gift card, as it was only good on the US Amazon, not the UK Amazon.

I\'m not ungrateful- $100 of free books is great, even if there are limitations. But why do those limitations exist? It\'s the same company, just a different country. I haven\'t really looked into the legal complications, so perhaps there\'s a good reason why they legally can\'t allow us to use both sites. However, to a layman just using the site, it seems a bit unfair that although I\'m allowed to buy products from the two (separate, yes, yet identical down to, for all intents and purposes, the logo) sites using the same log-in name, I can\'t use my gift card on both.

Like I said, maybe it\'s nit-picky. Other than that, though, gift cards are, as one would expect, very good.']

review_titles_seq: ["Does Anyone Else Feel Like They've Been ROBBED By Amazon???"]
review_texts_seq: ["I purchased six $50 Amazon Gift Cards from a local supermarket (Bi Lo) to give as Christmas Gifts in 2015 (something I've done for many years). My Sister-in-law, the recipient of one of those $50 Amazon Gift Cards called me to say that she's lost the Gift Card (most likely accidentally discarded with all of the Christmas paper, etc. and burned in the trash). I told her "no problem", since I had kept my receipt from Bi Lo that includes the Amazon Gift Card Number, and I felt certain that Amazon would be able to see that no purchases had been made against their Gift Card Number and that either Amazon or Bi Lo would be able to cancel that card and issue a new one, or Credit her online Amazon Account $50 and bypass issuing a new physical card altogether. I was sadly mistaken.... when she initially contacted Amazon, they told her that since the Amazon Card was purchased from Bi Lo, we would need to take the matter up with them. I went to Bi Lo and was told that there wasn't anything that they could do and that I would need to contact Amazon. Since my Sister-in-law had already contacted Amazon and been turned away, I decided since I was the one who made the purchase and had the receipt, I would call my Credit Card Company first to see if they might be able to offer some assistance in getting the matter resolved since I had purchased all of the Gift Cards with my Credit Card. After 30 minutes discussing the details with my Credit Card Company, they said they understood my dilemma but weren't able to dispute the charge with Bi Lo. They suggested I contact Amazon directly since I had my receipt with Amazon's Gift Card number on and since it was Amazon's gift card. So... after about 30 minutes on the phone with a very nice gentleman from Amazon who made 2 attempts to get his Supervisor to approve some type of credit for the loss, he sadly informed me that Amazon isn't responsible for purchases of their Gift Cards that aren't made from their website. I told him that since Amazon isn't willing to offer any assistance, even though they can clearly see in their system a $50 unused Credit on that lost Gift Card and since I had my receipt with their Gift Card number printed on the receipt (proof that I had purchased their Gift Card), I felt as though Amazon had ROBBED me of $50, since the only one who will benefit financially from this gift transaction is Amazon and I had certainly not intended to add "Amazon" as one of my 2015 Christmas names to buy for! Furthermore, I told him that I would not be making any more purchases from Amazon directly or purchasing any other Amazon Gift Cards in the future and would encourage others to do the same. I try not to support businesses that engage in thievery, and that is exactly how I feel I was treated in this instance."]

["I like the ease of Amazon gift cards, when it comes to the giving and receiving. But I have to agree with the other Prime members. I am sick and tired of watching my gift cards disappear because they are being applied to 1. orders from other members of my household (who don't know to update the order page or have placed orders via the next two methods). 2. Our subscribe and save items. 3. Any digital 1-click purchases.

I looked everywhere to find a way to change this method of automatically applying payments to a gift card balance, but unless using the regular check out for certain orders, Amazon does not provide a place to change this payment method. It is automatic. So I never get to use my gifts on myself. Since I'm not alone in this, I don't know if I'll be buying them for anybody with a Prime account or a household that shares an Amazon account in the future. And if I do decide to reload my balance, I'll have to remember the balance likely won't be used to buy myself something nice. But will be used for household purchases, which eliminates a certain amount of convenience and is one of the two reasons I have given this purchase only 3 stars. The other reason is that it took several hours for this reload to be reflected in my gift card balance, though the $5.00 credit I was offered was immediately applied.

I am usually very happy with my Amazon purchases and the services I subscribe to. So this is an unfortunate turn of events that I hope Amazon will quickly rectify for all account holders. I doubt very much that Amazon wants its customers to resent the gifts they are receiving through its company."]

In addition to the financial benefits, Amazon Reload is also incredibly convenient. I can easily reload my gift card balance directly from the Amazon app on my phone, and the funds are available to use immediately. This is especially helpful when I'm running low on funds and need to make an urgent purchase.

Another feature that I appreciate about Amazon Reload is the ability to set up automatic reloads. I can choose a specific reload amount and frequency, and Amazon will automatically add the funds to my gift card balance. This ensures that I always have funds available for future purchases and helps me stay within my budget.

Overall, Amazon Reload is an excellent service that provides both convenience and financial benefits. I highly recommend it to anyone who frequently shops on Amazon."]

['My Wife and I ordered a one year subscription from them for the Ice Cream of the month club. Our first 4 pints came and we were very pleased. We did get batch Ice Cream from lesser known creameries/shops within the United States. Most of the offerings were pretty good, one was FANTASTIC. The second shipment arrived, this time two were tame in comparison to the initial delivery, one was unique and the other was again, AWESOME. It was delivery number 3 that was terrible. Instead of small batch, craft-esque, unique Ice Cream, we got 4 pints that carried an Amazing Clubs brand and packaging. The flavors were not unique, they tasted terrible and I contacted amazing clubs. I explained the let down through email support. I was given a canned answer, something like " Were very sorry you did not enjoy your selection, we\'ll take your comments and discuss with our elfs" ....something like that. I don\'t know if I called or not. The RUB here is the guarantee that you\'ll love it. It\'s SUPER MISLEADING. I don\'t think you should ever "eat the steak" then complain and try to get something for free, but on the surface to a lay person wanting a "push" to purchase that there\'s some kind of Guarantee, it\'s a fair assumption that the guarantee would be for the dislike of the product. This is my hang-up and why the advertising is quasi DECEITFUL. I got my fourth and final order on 2/3/2021. I opened the box and got four generic, house branded Ice Creams. NOT UNIQUE, NOT CRAFT OR SMALL BATCH. The same crappy, uninteresting, boring pints. Mint Oreo, Chocolate Brownie, Carmel Coconut and Butter Pecan (which was damaged) cracked lid and ice cream coming out of container. It\'s what it is, it was meant to be fun but unfortunately it was only 2 shipments out of four that we had fun with. I thought after my email that I sent they may have taken into consideration selecting something much better, but they didn\'t. They fail at customer service, they let me down on what was something exciting by not continuing with their initial momentum. Had all deliveries been from unique places with wild flavors all the way through my subscription I wouldn\'t have hesitated to re-up my subscription. It\'s too bad. Now to address one more thought, the person who replies to all the complaints is not cool. The written sentiment to others that the author THINKS is amusing or snarky is really just belittling, berating and rude. I know consumers aren\'t always right, but a complaint of any kind shouldn\'t be handled like that. The author who responds to complaints reminds me of the kids who were the type to stand by the front doors of their own homes, curse at me, flip me the bird and when I\'d begin to approach they\'d run inside. ['Amazon emailed me (see image) practically demanding that I review this product, because my "opinion matters!"

So as long as you\'re finding this opinion of mine so important as to read it, I can tell you that this product did exactly as expected, reload funds to my amazon gift card balance, which I then spent like I\'d stolen them.

I actually used it because it was less of a hassle to use a one-time debit card I received for my teen\'s contact lens purchase as a rebate to reload the exact amount on the card to my Amazon gift card balance, and then spend that balance a little at a time, than to try and find a combination of purchases including tax which would equal the balance of the rebate card exactly to the penny.

So this "product" accomplished my little rebate card laundering task perfectly. Sadly, I wasn\'t able to multiply my money as a result, and they didn\'t send me a pot of gold, like the leprechaun reload service promised me, nor another ten point four million dollurs like my friend the prince of Nigeria claimed, plus if I had spent the money on buying stock index shares, I could\'ve lost it in the recent market crashes instead, so perhaps this wasn\'t the best or least method of moving money around, but I still have lucky charms in my pantry and toilet paper in my bathroom cabinets, so there\'s that, and they can\'t take that away from you, unless you don\'t pay your property taxes.

I particularly enjoyed rating this reload from one to five stars on "comfort". I of course, had to give it five stars, because it\'s like a puffy cloud on an otherwise clear summer\'s day, where from afar it looks soft and pure, but if you\'d ever walked through one, as on a mountain-top, or the wing of a biplane, you\'d realize it\'s actually more like a wet sneeze.

My cats enjoyed it. After all, they prefer tight fits (evidence in attached photo), as opposed to fit tights, which they have more of a tendency to rip to nylon shreds, as they\'ve never been de-clawed, despite their status as ragdolls.

If you\'re wondering why there are multiple copies of the same book on the top shelf of the image, and some of them say "Not for Resale" on the spine, that\'s because I\'m the author and those are first editions as well as proof copies.

Which is where we come full circle, because once "reloaded" onto my Amazon gift card balance, I spent the money on author\'s copies of my books from Amazon, some of which remain on that shelf, and others of which I signed and shipped to the fans who won my launch contest.

And you thought this whole thing didn\'t have an actual point, like a #2 pencil which has been stored in a jar at the SAT testing center for anyone to wield, but it did, like a rapier which has been used to stab the court wit.']

The UPS delivery person dropped off the boxes at 6:30pm on December 21, 2011 @ their front door without ringing the door bell or knocking at the door. It was dark already, both boxes were stolen, the thief took the cards and threw the empty boxes @ a neighbor's front door. I can't believe when I heard my son told me that the outside of the box has large print which reads AMAZON GIFT CARDS!! Who in the world will do such a dumb thing?

After talking to an Amazon reprsentative, my credit card account was credited for $200.00. The representative could not answer my question regarding whether the giftcard has any log in requirements before using it. I like Amazon, but I will never purchase any Amazon Giftcards by mail again. I have never mailed any giftcards to anybody and I will never do that either!! Do it electronically!! Lesson learned."]

In conclusion, Amazon Reload has truly been an excellent choice for me. Its convenience, cash back rewards, and security benefits have made my online shopping experience even more enjoyable. review_titles_seq: ['Register it online before you can use it online']
review_texts_seq:
["I needed to spend some money on a credit card that has a UK billing address, which can be difficult as a lot of online stores don't allow foreign billing addresses. And most sites that sell Visa gift cards also don't accept foreign billing addresses themselves. But Amazon does, so I bought this Visa gift card on Amazon, paid for it with the UK card, problem solved.

I didn't use this card in any physical stores, so I can't speak to that experience. I received it today, immediately registered it at the URL that's on the back of the card (top right, small text). You need to register it online first to be able to make purchases with it online (this is how you set your name and billing address on it, which you would need for any online order).

I then used it on Etsy.com and Mouth.com for purchases that came close to the $100. I then used it to reload my Amazon gift card balance in the amount that I had left. I then checked my balance again at the same website where I had registered it, and indeed it showed my three transactions and correct zero balance. No problems at any point."]

review_titles_seq: ['Elegant Gift for the Amazon lover - No gift wrap required']
review_texts_seq:
["I recently gifted this to a family member for Christmas, and was very pleased with the delivery.

Here's why to get this:

1. If you're going to get an Amazon gift card, why not get a gift card which is wrapped in an elegant little box and is guaranteed to be delivered within one business day for FREE? The card arrived on time, and with the guaranteed delivery, I knew I could time it to be exactly right for the occasion rather than taking a chance of being too early or too late by mail.

2. It saved me the hassle of gift wrapping it. Don't bother with the 'gift wrap' option during checkout either. The box is elegantly wrapped as it is.

3. It came in a large envelope rather than a full blown Amazon box, so the family member really didn't have a clue as to what it was until she opened her box.

4. The variety of gift card designs that you can pick from that can be boxed gives you the flexibility to choose the right card for your occassion.

5. My gift recipient is a huge Kindle fan. With the gift card, she got herself some books that she enjoyed rather than some odd gift I might have picked. She also shopped for some other stuff on Amazon that she would not have otherwise. So needless to say, this gift worked well for her.

If you were gifting this to someone in person rather than having it delivered, then you may want to get a small greeting card to place inside the box as an identifier. There is no place to note your name or greetings on the box itself. This isn't a fault. It's what you expect from a great gift box."]

review_titles_seq: ['Rest Assured, This Is Indeed a $25 Gift Card in a Black Gift Box']
review_texts_seq:
["At first, I was skeptical. Would this gift card be exactly $25? What if they only gave me $24.75 and tried to pull it off as $25? What if the box wasn't the right shade of black? Was it going to be jet black, onyx, or obsidian? Would the bow be off-center? To be honest, it looked a little off-center in the photo. What if I went to type in the gift card code, lost my memory, forgot how to operate a keyboard, and never recovered my hard-earned money? We've all had these doubts -- it's only human.

I'm happy to say that the bow -- just gold enough to hint at prestige with a touch of yellow that says "I'm also fun!" -- was immaculately placed. I assume machine learning was involved (God bless you, Mr. Bezos). The interior of the box, which may look to be little more than black cardboard, is in fact black cardboard covered in a thin, felt-like veneer. Teasing the card from its luxurious case, I scratched away the code with my full mental faculties intact. At last, 408 digits later, the screen read "$25.00". Not $24.75, not $24.95, but a full twenty-five American dollars.

It is no exaggeration to say that, if only for a moment, my faith in humanity has been restored."]

review_texts_seq:
['I make most purchases here with a credit card, so the Amazon Gift Card is not a regular payment method for my routine purchases. What it *does* provide me is a dumping ground for almost every other hard to use gift card — presents, store refunds, promotional rebates, participation incentives, etc. It can be a pain to track a pile of cards, which can expire, are hard to drain of "change" from a partial use, and some merchants will discourage or refuse a split payment. I\'ve lost significant money to those challenges, and spend too much emotional energy trying to avoid the traps.

Now I immediately dump any gift card I receive into the Amazon card, knowing that sooner or later I will have a purchase to make. No lost cards. Nothing lost to fees or expiration or loose change. No problem with use limitations. Yay! It is also a faster way to receive credit for returns to Amazon than waiting for the bank to issue credit, or having 3rd-party vendors complicate the process.

The gift card is automatically the default payment choice for my next purchase — so I don\'t forget and have money sitting in an unused credit. But if I *don\'t* want to use it (from a different budget category, or money I owe to somebody else), I can change the default choice and hold the gift card balance for whatever time or purpose.

The process is sort of not intuitive and it\'s easy to lose where things are on the Amazon site, but once figured out it\'s swell. I would take a rating star or half star for ease of use — but I know of no alternative with similar utility, so it sits at the top of its class. However many stars that should be.']

review_titles_seq: ['A GREAT (and SAFER & MORE PRIVATE!) Alternative to Using Your Own Credit Card for Online Shopping!']
review_texts_seq:
['I got this [[ASIN:B01MSBQB1P $100 Visa Gift Card]] because although I have actual credit/debit cards that I use in person at brick & mortar stores and other businesses and online on big-name websites like Amazon, Instacart, Shipt, Target and the like, I am not comfortable giving out my actual card info when shopping on less(er) known and/or potentially risky websites.

So when circumstances necessitate doing business with them (as it did recently, while looking for a replacement battery for my 2007 HP laptop I dug out from a closet after not using it since 2009-2010 [and particularly since switching to Apple/Mac in 2012-2013] in order to play some retro offline Windows games I\'ve not played in years that I missed playing................unfortunately, neither Amazon nor any other big-name stores or websites [like Best Buy, NewEgg, etc.] seem to carry a compatible battery and I had to go with an unknown/lesser known website) I prefer to use non-reloadable prepaid "gift" cards, so that in the worst case scenario, if the site is "fly-by-night" scam business and/or the website gets hacked, they won\'t have access to my actual credit/debit card info or bank data, and the maximum amount of money I\'d potentially lose would limited to whatever the denomination (or remaining balance) on the prepaid card. Granted, depending on the card (AFAIK there cards come in denominations of $25, $50, $100 and $200 cards) it could still be a lot of money to lose, but at least one\'s entire credit line and private info wouldn\'t be at risk as it would be using a conventional credit/debit card.

Personally, after several years of using prepaid Visa, Mastercard and other credit cards, like this one, I have to say I think prepaid "gift" cards are a GREAT option, when shopping online, especially when making purchases at certain websites/kinds of websites.

However, previously, Amazon did NOT offer these prepaid Visa, Mastercard and other credit-card "gift" cards and rather, only offered gift cards for specific stores, restaurants or other businesses. This necessitated having to physically go to a brick & mortar store and buy a prepaid "gift" credit card in person anytime I needed a Visa/Mastercard to use online -- and since, due to disabilities, I\'m unable to drive, getting these prepaid cards were a huge hassle!

Which is why I am so glad that Amazon has started offering these prepaid Visa/Mastercard gift cards for sale through their site. I don\'t know if its because of COVID-19, and the lockdowns, or what, but making these prepaid cards available through Amazon, has made it a LOT easier for those of us who are mostly homebound, to get and use these cards as needed.

As mentioned, these cards come in denominations of $25, $50, $100 and $200, and are NOT reloadable (meaning once the balance on the card is used up, you need to buy another card and cannot add more money to that same card). Also they cannot be used to get cash at ATMs or POS (point of sale) purchases. But they can be made for most other purchases where Visa and Mastercard are accepted, which these days, is the majority of places, at least in the US. I have never used these in other countries, not even Canada, so I cannot speak to their functionality abroad. That being said, I recently tried to use one of these cards online on GOG (Good Old Games) and I had difficulty completing the transaction because apparently the site\'s based in Europe, so the card was declined. But then I just made the payment using the card as a "guest" via Paypal (I no longer trust Paypal enough to maintain an actual account with them anymore) and the transaction went through, immediately.

Other than that, I\'ve had no problems with these cards. The card arrives, open the package and register the card number on their listed website, with your basic info (name, address, phone number, email) which AFAIK is NOT necessary for in-person purchases, but IS (or may be) necessary for online purchases -- and then use the card just like you would any other Visa or Mastercard until you\'ve exhausted the amount on your card. Then, throw it away (or cut it up first if you\'ve registered it with your personal info) and get another one the next time you need it!

Easy-peasy!

⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ 5 STARS!!!!!!!!!']

["I purchased these gift cards as part of a promotion Amazon was running. I will upload a photo of the email I received. In the email it stated "Get $15.00 Amazon credit with a $50 Amazon gift card purchase". It's the end of the school year, so I purchased 3 $50.00 gift card for my kids teachers. I figured that was a great deal for both of us, I spend $35.00 and they get $50.00 for their classroom.

Four days later I attempt to purchase a birthday present and was reminded to check on my $45.00 credit I thought I had coming. I couldn't find it, used all their "self help" links, and finally found a phone number to speak to a human and get help. First lady was wonderful, told me the reason I didn't get it was because I had purchased all three in one transaction, instead of 3. I thought that was silly so I asked for a supervisor.

The supervisor, Deo located in the Philippines, was the supervisor I was connected to. He informed me what the email really meant was ONE $15.00 credit for purchasing OVER $50.00 in gift cards. Clearly that email is open to interpretation. He said it was written in the terms and conditions...however when I tried to read them for myself I was sent to a different screen (picture attached). I asked to speak with his supervisor, to which he informed me he is the very top of the customer service center. I asked for his boss. He said he was only authorized to give me a mailing address. Dumbfounded I asked him if Amazon corporate office in Washington does not have phones or email. He said they are only allowed to contact them via their computer system.

Most of my conversation with Deo was in silence. I'm assuming he was typing up everything I was saying for amazon's records. 54 minutes into my conversation the line disconnected and they never called back. I called back to get amazon's address and was surprisingly connected to a customer service rep who worked in the same department as Deo. He spoke with Deo (who was unable to speak with me since he was busy with another customer). The new customer service rep, Ian, could not have been kinder and more professional. I felt like he was actually listening to my complaint verse Deo who just wanted to record every little thing I said.

Ian helped me get the contact information I needed, and also gave me the email address of where I could forward a copy of the email in question. Ian also provided me with the PO Box for Amazon Corporate Office in Seattle. Since I can not voice my compliant to Amazon corporate office directly, and I must write a letter, I figured I would share it with all who would listen. I hope your Amazon experience is better than mine. And Deo, you might want to pay attention to Ian and Mercy - they are customer service pros.

Long story short, Amazon - who is worth $430 BILLION - would rather lose a long time customer over $30. But as for the product, it was adorable and looked great in my candy bouquets. I'll attach a picture of that too."]

review_titles_seq: ['Kindle gift card only works for Kindle-related purchases.']
review_texts_seq:
['All I asked for this Christmas was Amazon gift cards. So a relative went to Best Buy to ask for one, and she was handed an Amazon Kindle Gift Card. I wasn\'t sure if this would work for general Amazon purchases, so I sent an e-mail to Amazon customer service. The reply I received from Amazon was that the Kindle Gift Card can only be used for Kindle-related purchases, NOT for Amazon general merchandise. I tried to take the card back to Best Buy to exchange it for a regular Amazon gift card (which is what she asked for from the sales associate, so apparently, even retailers are unaware of this policy, although when I returned the manager knew this probably because others were trying to return their Kindle gift cards). Anyway, the manager there said it cannot be returned or exchanged, and confirmed it can only be used to make Kindle-related purchases. He said this is an Amazon return policy, not a Best Buy policy.

Now the real question is, why would anyone in their right mind want an Amazon Kindle Gift Card with all these limitations, when they could get a regular Amazon gift card and buy anything at the Amazon store, including Kindle related purchases. This is a ridiculous policy, and if anyone says I\'m lying, I\'ll be happy to forward the e-mail I received from Amazon customer service concerning this issue.

*** UPDATE: Someone from Amazon called me to say if I first put the Amazon Kindle Gift Cards into my account using the number before making a purchase the money should be available for other purchases. They also sent me an e-mail with more specific instructions. Not sure if this is a rule change or what, but I appreciate them taking the time out to call me and leave another e-mail. I\'ll post the new e-mail below with the instructions (the first e-mail telling me it cannot be used this way is in the comments discussion to this review). Kudos to Amazon for listening to their customers if this is true (And I assume it is). I have not used the cards yet, and hadn\'t even scratched the off the cover over the numbers because I was thinking about trying to have Amazon exchange them for regular Amazon gift cards. Anyway, I\'ll bump up my rating to 3 stars (minus 2 for the misinformation) and the new e-mail is below:

Hello Bill,

I\'m sorry for the misinformation you have previously received in an email from us about using your Gift Card for purchases on Amazon.com. I\'ve tried contacting you at the phone number listed in your Amazon.com account but have been unsuccessful.

To use an Amazon.com Gift Card (or a Gift Card with the Kindle name on it) for purchases from Amazon.com, visit Your Account (http://www.amazon.com/your-account) and look for the gift card option in the Payments section.

You can also enter your gift card claim code during checkout in the box labeled "Have any gift cards, gift certificates or promotional claim codes?" in the right column. If you use 1-Click ordering, you\'ll find a similar option if you click "Review or edit your 1-Click orders" after clicking "Buy now with 1-Click" on a product\'s page.

You\'ll find more instructions here:

http://www.amazon.com/help/giftcards

If you still need help, you can contact us via phone, chat, or e-mail by clicking the "Contact Us" button on any Help page (http://www.amazon.com/help).

I hope this helps! We look forward to seeing you again soon.

Megan']

review_titles_seq: ['I normally hate gift cards, but Amazon gift cards are okay', 'Wasteful but nice if the person will reuse the tin']
review_texts_seq:
["When people give me gift cards, it's often a chore to use them. I forget to carry them with me, I buy something but forget there was a gift card in my wallet, they expire or start deducting fees if you don't use them right away, or in the worst case I can't find anything that I want or need from that particular store. It's also a pain trying to keep track of how much is left on each card and what you spent it on.

On the flip side, sometimes when I do remember that I have a gift card, I feel almost obligated to spend the gift card on something nice instead of on my normal purchases like personal hygiene products and food--you know, because the person who gave me the gift card probably didn't envision buying me deodorant and eggs. (But then again, maybe they thought I could use some deodorant and thought giving it to me directly would be too rude.)

Aside from these generalities, I have a few specific thoughts on certain types of gift cards.

Restaurant gift cards: Of all the gift cards I get, restaurant gift cards are the easiest to use. Either I get to try a new restaurant that I haven't visited before, or I get treated to a meal or two at one of my favorite places. I take my wife out to dinner and use the gift card in one or two visits. If there will only be a few bucks on the gift card after our meal and tip, we usually add drinks and/or dessert.

Best Buy: I hate Best Buy. Fortunately, nobody gives me Best Buy gift cards.
Kmart: I don't normally go to Kmart, but at least I can go there to convert a Sears gift card into a Red Lobster gift card.
Lowes: I buy a ton of stuff at Lowe's so I definitely use those gift cards, but it's disappointing to me if I end up spending the gift card on a bunch of random little supplies instead of on tools or on a larger project.
Sears: I hate Sears and the closest one is more than an hour away.
Target: I don't normally go to Target
Walmart: Normally I just buy small, random, everyday stuff

AMEX/Visa/Mastercard prepaid debit cards: Don't get me started! These things are the biggest pain of all. I've had Visa and Mastercard prepaid debit cards and gift cards that wouldn't go through on a purchase on numerous occasions, and by the time I thought to try using them again, they were expired or all the funds had been consumed by monthly service fees. Although legislation has since been passed which outlaws such fees, I still can't stand the idea that the person buying the gift card has to pay an activation charge. Whenever I get these cards, I've now learned to either apply them to my Amazon account (if it actually goes through) or cell phone bill immediately.

Amazon: the best thing about Amazon gift cards is that I already buy a lot of stuff from Amazon. In a way, I feel like a sucker for spending so much at Amazon after starting my Prime subscription a couple years ago, but as it happens, Amazon also has the best prices (or close to it) anyway on a lot of the stuff I buy.

The only downside to Amazon gift cards (and it's kind of a big one for me) is that it's really easy to unintentionally eat up your gift cards without realizing it. Case in point: the other week I applied a gift card to my Amazon account. A couple days later, I rented a movie, which was charged against my gift card credit. When I went to buy something else, I thought I would be partially paying it with the gift card credit but the amount paid by gift card was less than I expected. I was about to write Amazon's customer service to complain, but then I looked at my gift card history and could see very plainly where the money left.

It is because of this purchase history feature alone that I'm comfortable giving Amazon gift cards a 4-star rating. If it weren't for that, I would probably just give them a 3-star rating (at best) because of my overall annoyance with gift cards in general.", "I kind of felt bad buying a gift card in a tin because it seems wasteful to me, but my mom is all about presentation and I thought this would be a little more fun than just giving a boring gift card to go with her new Roku XS. To make it a little more fun, I froze it in a block of ice, which she thought was cute--Santa being from the north pole, and all. She'll probably reuse the tin to give another gift card to someone else, so I guess it's not all bad.

A lot of other customers said their gift card boxes were shipped in a padded envelope and arrived all beat up. Apparently Amazon did notice the complaints, because mine was shipped in a cardboard box with the inflatable air pouches and arrived in perfect condition."]

["I received this gift card through an Amazon promotion. It arrived promptly and in a fairly large, sealed envelope. I was intending to give the gift card as a Christmas gift for a family member and wanted to be sure there was an actual gift card inside. I didn't want to destroy the outer envelope for fear that was Amazon's intended packaging for the gift card. The brief fret was unnecessary. Amazon has the large sealed envelope protecting another envelope and a card. The gift card is attached to the card (the presentation is pretty much like the photo on the product page). The gift card itself was a hard plastic card. I don't know if Amazon still issues its paper gift certificates but this is a definite improvement as it is less prone to damage by water or tearing. A nice gift that is well packaged.", 'What\'s that? You forgot to get a gift for the cousin that you never see but who will be present at the holiday gathering? You pulled Bob\'s name in Secret Santa and you know nothing about Bob? You detest shopping? Look no further than this handy ten pack of Amazon gift cards.

Here are some facts about the gift cards:

1)What would I be handing to my gift recipient? These gift cards are the traditional plastic kind. Also note that Amazon sells gift cards in various formats. You can get gift certificates that you print at home, e-gift cards delivered via Facebook, and e-gift cards delivered by email.

2)How are the gift cards packaged? You get a stack of ten cards that come in a single, fully closed (non-zipper) plastic bag that must be torn open in order to remove the cards. My stack of gift cards arrived in a nondescript bubble wrap mailer.

3)Does the buyer receive envelopes or greeting cards? You receive no envelopes and you receive no greeting cards. Amazon does have an option where you can buy a single gift card that comes with an envelope and greeting card. review_titles_seq: ['Card ok if you can put up with Amazon.com customer service']
review_texts_seq:
['If you\'ve never had a problem shopping from Amazon.com, then you really are not experienced enough to be giving the "gift" of Amazon to someone else. Wait until you\'ve experienced your first screw up, and then evaluate.

I received a gift certificate, but have had trouble using it, because Amazon.com\'s outsourced customer service does not handle issues well. They are apparently scripted to say that an appropriate person will contact you within 48 hours, but in my experience, follow up contact is not timely. When contact is made, it has been to tell me that the issue was not well documented by the prior agents and to start over explaining my concern once again. After that, I was told, once more, to wait 48 hours for follow-up that did not come. Rinse and repeat.

The problem is that Amazon.com has apparently fire-walled these folks in Bangalore (or some other asian town) from the rest of the company. Therefore, there can be no quick responses to customer concerns. For me, after five contacts, I spoke with a "team lead" who indicated that prior agents had not documented the subject matter of my prior calls (even though I was promised a pompt resolution by those agents).

Add to all this the fact that during the recent holiday season, Amazon.com raised the price of the item I wished to purchase more than once, at the same time that the item\'s manufacturer was offering it for considerably less. This makes having my "gift" money tied up in an Amazon.com account less than ideal.

Do not expect that the person to whom you intend to give a gift will not have to deal with the customer service department. Try to be forward-thinking enough to consider that a problem might occur. If it does, the recipient will likely have a very negative experience, regardless of the variety of products offered by Amazon.com.

When I asked an Amazon.com customer service agent why Amazon.com was charging 150% of what the manufacturer was selling the product for directly, I was told that the additional expense should be considered to cover the expert customer service available at Amazon.com. This is terribly amusing, considering that the only thing that the agents tend to do is instruct the customer to wait 48 hours for someone else to address the problem (which, in my experience, does not happen).

If you are set on letting someone choose their own gift, you should consider a pre-paid Visa or Mastercard. That way, the recipient could use the funds at Amazon.com if he or she so chooses, and is still free to purchase something locally from a person who could not avoid responding to a customer\'s concerns.']

review_titles_seq: ['A complete rip-off. Avoid like the plague.']
review_texts_seq:
["I can't argue strongly enough against these things. My son got me one for my birthday, which was sweet as heck of him - and the next chance I got, we made plans to go see a movie together. When I arrived at the theater and tried to actually *use* the card, however, I found that you can't do so - the card has to be activated somehow (yet when you go to the fandango site and try to do anything along those lines, all it does is give you a list of movies). In other words, the only way, apparently, you can actually *use* the card is to order your tickets online ahead of the showing.

So, if you aren't positive of which movie you're going to see before you head out, you're out of luck. Given that I don't always know precisely how long it's going to take for us to get all the way across town to the theater, this is an asinine hoop to jump through. Either we can block out an extra hour to see our movie - and sit through forty five minutes of obnoxious, inescapable TV commercials that we *pay* to endure - or I can't use the heartfelt gift my kid gave me. Poor guy spent his own money because he wanted to see a movie with his dad to celebrate my birthday, and, quite frankly, I feel like he got ripped off.

If you want to give a movie-going gift, I'd suggest pretty much anything other than this. See if the theater has gift certificates. Give a pre-paid visa card. Anything. It's absurd that a gift card - which was paid for with cash - is about as convenient to use as an expired discount coupon you cut out of the back of a cereal box.

UPDATE: I finally used the cards by ordering some tickets online - and had to pay a CONVENIENCE FEE ON TOP OF EVERYTHING ELSE. Yes, for the non-convenience of not even being able to USE these unless I order ahead of time, four bucks of my son's cash was just sucked into the great aether. I'll never voluntarily give Fandango a dime of my money ever again. My kid is awesome. Fandango isn't."]

Bait & Switch by Amazon: Get a $10 credit when you send a $50 Amazon Gift Card by text message
Reviewed in the United States on October 10, 2017
Subject: Get a $10 credit when you send a $50 Amazon Gift Card by text message

If you received that promotion email from Amazon, be very careful. My purchase experience with that promotion felt like a "bait & switch" by Amazon website. I clicked on the promotion email link and tried to buy a $50 gift card. I entered the phone number for texting the gift card and as I clicked "Buy Now" button, Amazon website reloaded the gift-card purchase page & prompted me to enter an email address because the delivery option was changed (by Amazon) to "Deliver by Email".

I was confused and tried it to start over two more times. Both times, after I entered a phone number where the gift card would be delivered to, and clicked on "Buy Now" button, Amazon website would reload the page and change to "Deliver by Email". Somewhat out of patience, I just proceeded to enter an email and completed the whole purchase.

After reading the fine print of this promotion, I realized that $10 credit is given only when the $50 gift card is delivered by text to a phone number.

To me, the whole experience is a "bait & switch". I wanted to buy $50 gift card and I followed the email link & entered a phone number. As I wanted to pay for the purchase, Amazon website changed the delivery option to "Deliver by Email" to mislead me into entering an email address to deliver the gift card. In turn, that would disqualify me for the $10 credit.']

Disappointed, I contacted the seller to have the card devalued and another one sent. I wasn't given a tracking number on the second one, which is understandable because it costs, like, a dollar to add that to a package. After two months of occasionally asking my family if they've gotten anything in the mail the card never got there and my sister is still without a gift. I would have been better off sending her a video of me burning $20.

While I can't say for sure whose fault it is, it does seem a little fishy that both cards failed to arrive. With my luck the devalued card will show up a month from now and my sister will go to the store and leave disappointed.

['I had a small stack of used giftcards sitting around. You know, when the balance gets to like $2.34, and you don\'t know what to do with them? Easy to "recharge gift balance" with all of those cards sitting around!

1. Look up the balance.
2. Click Account & Lists
3. Select Gift Cards
4. Click the yellow "Reload Your Balance" button
5. Enter Gift Card balance under the $(Other) block.
6. Click Buy Now
7. Under Payment Method, Select Change and enter gift card information.
8. Verify and click "Place Order"

You can repeat with all of your applicable gift cards. Just remember to go through and clean up your payment methods when you are done, so you don\'t have 13 random debit cards to choose from in the future.']

review_titles_seq: ['Uploading $600 using my credit card to my account requires verification I wasn’t aware about.']
review_texts_seq:
['Sent a $600 gift card to my account to be made for future purchases using my credit card. The transaction on the surface appeared seamless, received an automated email thanking me and informing me that I should see the new/updated account balance within five minutes.

That didn’t happen, instead about an hr later I get a call from a Seattle Washington number. Not knowing who it was, but suspecting it may be Amazon I just let my phone buzz. I really do not like answering my phone when I don’t know who or what is on the other end. Anyway I was left a message that was all but beyond recognizable, the only word I understood was “amazon”. Tried calling back, but of course amazon uses a random phone number generator, so all I get is an automated response telling me the number I dialed isn’t found to be in service.

I then try to find someone to contact (is it just me that has a little trouble finding amazon’s CSR information on this site?) after going through a couple of page levels I find the necessary steps that are needed to have someone directly contact me. I enter my phone number so someone can call me. I have a tendency to ramble on when it comes to writing/typing a complaint but a bit briefer when talking to an actual human being. I get another Seattle WA call, this time I answer it straightaway. The person on the other line named “Jeena” sounds friendly enough, but I get a quickly growing suspicion she has an amazon CSR help manual/script along with an Hindi-to-English dictionary in front of her as she is speaking to me.

I explain to her everything that had transpired thus far. She expresses her concern but does little to alleviate them or to ameliorate my current situation. Through several distractions on the other end I can barely make heads or tails on what Jeena is trying to convey to me and need to ask several times for clarification. What I gathered from the conversation was the following, that I should see my account updated with the $600 within 12hrs. She also suggested that I try loading an additional smaller amount, like $100 to my account to se if it goes through. I explained that I didn’t feel comfortable sending more currency over into my account when I had the amount that I already sent having not yet gone through. She more or less shared my concerns, but whether or not she was just being sincere or simply parroting is anyone’s guess. I’m going for the latter.

Anyway the conversation lasted longer than I would have liked, ended with me getting her name and a promise to have her call me back. That has yet to happen, I’m afraid that my amazon CSR like basically every lady I’ve met has stood me up, lol.

So as of 3/12/2019 I haven’t had any updates, with the minor exception of an email from Jeena promising to call me to follow up on seeing whether or not my account reflects the necessary changes.

This has been and still is being an aggravating experience. Their is nothing that I could find in the riveting-edge-of-your-seat-easy-to-follow-totally-not-a-boilerplated-lopsided read of their ToS or policies regarding the limit or ammount you could transfer before they get suspicious. I see no reason why, my credit card that I have saved on my own account for quick transactions should have amazon not allowing this to go through.

UPDATE: while in the middle of writing this review Jeena called me back. Nothing has yet to be resolved. With a frustrating mixture of trying to calmly as possible voice my frustration while at the same time knowing just how frustrated this has made me I went through basically the same talk I had about 24hrs ago.

She explained to me for security reasons that I needed to be verified, though explains nothing of what such a process entails. After explaining to her for the umptieth time that verification isn’t an issue of some arbitrary allotted amount of time but simply of verification I am all but exhausted in this endeavor. I half-jokingly explained after she explained to me Amazon’s reasoning behind this. In the past people hacked into other people accounts to I guess upload gift card amounts then claim said amount was stolen or sent to the wrong account.

So basically what I said was “Let me try to understand this. What you’re telling me Jeena is that amazon sees that I sent a $600 amazon gift card using my credit card to my own account, an account I’ve had with the same email address since 2011, and wants to know that I’m actually ‘me’ and not simply pretending to be ‘me’? And in order to verify ‘me’ from ‘me’ some arbitrary amount of time needs to be allotted that somehow gives them the correct answer to my alleged self-identity theft?” Confused? I sure am!

Amazon needs to update their policies by giving them crystal clear clarity on the amount you can transfer before they get suspicious. Also the point is ultimately moot, since as I explained to Jeena I could have uploaded the entire amount in increments within 2hrs without amazon freezing my account. Suspiciously high amount of transactions in their (Amazon’s) mind should be no different than smaller ones when it comes to fraudulence. It should be the onus of the customer to contact amazon regarding fraudulent or suspicious activity regarding their own accounts. We should have enough agency & responsibility when it comes to managing our own accounts.

I don’t need amazon not telling me how much I can spend, then telling me the amount I transacted using my own card for my own account has enter the level of possible fraudulence. As if there is some actual capstone or touchstone when it comes to when a transaction becomes suspicious or suspected of fraudulence!

This has been so far a highly disappointing ordeal:(']

['After redesigning a workflow process, I think everyone will agree that it should be easier and less confusing. Amazon has managed to do the opposite!
